---
title: "Distance to school"
subtitle: "In straight lines, and then on real streets and bus timetables: do children in deprived neighbourhoods live further from a secondary school than their neighbours, where is that unusual, and does absence go with it?"
---

```{r setup}
#| include: false
source(here::here("R", "site_helpers.R"))
library(patchwork); library(ggrepel)
D <- readRDS(here::here("data", "distance.rds"))
BH <- "Brighton and Hove"
dd <- D$districts; la <- D$authorities
km <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f km", x)
kms <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)
dv <- function(p, col) dd[[col]][dd$place == p]
cv <- function(p, col) D$compare[[col]][D$compare$place == p]
pcf <- function(r) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * (r - 1))
nd <- nrow(dd)
fsh <- 100 * mean(dd$ratio > 1)
urb <- dd |> filter(kind == "Mostly urban"); nu <- nrow(urb)
fshu <- 100 * mean(urb$ratio > 1)
ula <- la |> filter(urban_share >= 80)
bh_ula <- rank(-ula$near_dep, ties.method = "min")[ula$place == BH]
med_la <- median(la$near_dep)
lm_b <- function(g, s, col = "b") { x <- D$la_models; x[[col]][x$group == g & x$spec == s] }
S1 <- "Given the share disadvantaged and how urban"; S2 <- "And without London"
bh_near <- la$near_dep[la$place == BH]
imp <- function(g, s) (bh_near - med_la) * lm_b(g, s)
bh_gap_eng <- la$abs_dis[la$place == BH] - D$eng_abs$abs_dis
kn <- function(o, col = "b") D$kinds[[col]][D$kinds$outcome == o]
kp <- function(o, p, col = "b") { x <- D$kinds_place; x[[col]][x$outcome == o & x$place == p] }
ex <- function(p, col = "b") D$sch_excess[[col]][D$sch_excess$place == p]
rs <- function(g, ab) D$results$b[D$results$group == g & D$results$absence_in_model == ab]
wi <- function(s, col) D$whatif[[col]][startsWith(D$whatif$scenario, s)]
ck <- function(s, p, col) D$checks[[col]][D$checks$spec == s & D$checks$lad == p]
UR <- "Urban, near a major town or city"; UF <- "Urban, further from one"; RU <- "Rural"
PLACE_COL <- setNames(c(DPURPLE, BPURPLE, BLUE), c(UR, UF, RU))
THIRD_COL <- c("Most deprived third" = BPURPLE, "Other neighbourhoods" = DPURPLE)
# How firm is the link? R/19_distance_absence.R
R <- readRDS(here::here("data", "distance_absence.rds"))
GRL <- c(dis = "Disadvantaged", non = "Non-disadvantaged", all = "All pupils")
ylab <- function(tp) sprintf("%d/%02d", tp %/% 100L, tp %% 100L)
ci2 <- function(b, se) sprintf("%+.2f (%+.2f to %+.2f)", b, b - 1.96 * se, b + 1.96 * se)
oa <- function(g, added, s, col = "b") { x <- R$one_at_a_time; x[[col]][x$group == g & x$added == added & x$sample == s] }
oa_ci <- function(g, added, s) ci2(oa(g, added, s), oa(g, added, s, "se"))
pl <- function(out, ctl = "Share, urban", s = "All authorities", col = "b") { x <- R$pooled; x[[col]][x$out == out & x$control == ctl & x$sample == s] }
pl_ci <- function(out) ci2(pl(out), pl(out, col = "se"))
uc <- function(g, chk, col = "b") { x <- R$urban_checks; x[[col]][x$group == g & x$check == chk] }
us <- function(out, s = "Mostly urban, without London", col = "b") { x <- R$urban_step; x[[col]][x$out == out & x$sample == s] }
us2 <- function(g, col = "b") { x <- R$urb_sample; x[[col]][x$group == g & x$sample == "Less urban" & x$control == "Share, urban"] }
ckla <- function(g, chk, col) { x <- R$checks_la; x[[col]][x$group == g & x$check == chk] }
cl2 <- function(s, col) R$collinear[[col]][R$collinear$sample == s]
rc <- function(g, col, s = "All authorities") { x <- R$race; x[[col]][x$group == g & x$sample == s] }
shape_b <- function(g, band) { x <- R$shape; x$b[x$group == g & x$band == band] }
bw <- function(band, cmp, col = "b") { x <- R$between; x[[col]][x$band == band & x$comparison == cmp] }
bp <- function(band, ph, s, col = "b") { x <- R$band_place; x[[col]][x$band == band & x$phase == ph & x$sample == s] }
bp2 <- function(ph, col = "b") { x <- R$by_band; x[[col]][x$band == "Most deprived three tenths" & x$phase == ph] }
bk <- function(o, ph, col = "b") { x <- R$band_kinds; x[[col]][x$outcome == o & x$phase == ph] }
bk3 <- function(o) bk(o, "sec")
kl <- function(g, o, col = "b", s = "All authorities") { x <- R$kinds_la; x[[col]][x$group == g & x$outcome == o & x$sample == s] }
dc <- function(p, k, col) { x <- R$deciles; x[[col]][x$place == p & x$dec == k & x$phase == "sec"] }
cv_sec <- R$curve |> filter(phase == "sec"); cv_dis <- cv_sec |> filter(group == "dis")
yd <- R$by_year |> filter(group == "dis", control == "Share disadvantaged, how urban", sample == "All authorities")
sy <- function(tp0, col = "b") { x <- R$sch_year; x[[col]][x$outcome == "overall" & x$tp == tp0] }
sy_all <- R$sch_year |> filter(outcome == "overall")
fsf <- R$sch_fe |> filter(outcome == "overall")
gm <- function(g, set, s = "All authorities", col = "b") { x <- R$group_mix; x[[col]][x$group == g & x$set == set & x$sample == s] }
gm_ci <- function(g, set, s = "All authorities") ci2(gm(g, set, s), gm(g, set, s, "se"))
gterm <- "Ethnic mix of the group, the school population and residents"
gl <- function(g, term, s = "All authorities", col = "est") { x <- R$gel_tab; x[[col]][x$group == g & x$term == term & x$sample == s] }
we <- function(e, s, col = "b", ph = "sec", d = "From deprived neighbourhoods", ctl = "Share, urban") { x <- R$within_eth; x[[col]][x$eth == e & x$sample == s & x$phase == ph & x$distance == d & x$control == ctl] }
dm <- function(part, col = "b", s = "All authorities", ph = "sec") { x <- R$decomp_mix; x[[col]][x$part == part & x$sample == s & x$phase == ph] }
fm <- function(g, col, s = "All authorities") { x <- R$full_models; x[[col]][x$group == g & x$sample == s] }
gp <- function(g, out, s = "Mostly urban, without London", col = "b") { x <- R$group_mix_pri; x[[col]][x$group == g & x$out == out & x$sample == s] }
gk <- function(g, o, s = "Mostly urban, without London", col = "b") { x <- R$group_mix_kinds; x[[col]][x$group == g & x$outcome == o & x$sample == s] }
swp <- function(o, col) R$sch_wb_pool[[col]][R$sch_wb_pool$outcome == o]
pool_r <- gm("dis", "And every control", "Mostly urban, without London"); pool_s <- gm("dis", "And ethnic mix, region and density", "Mostly urban, without London")
J <- readRDS(here::here("data", "journey_times.rds"))
jt <- function(p, col, s = "walk_bus") J$places[[col]][J$places$place == p & J$places$scenario == s]
library(data.table)
SB <- readRDS(here::here("data", "school_buses.rds")); CB <- readRDS(here::here("data", "climb.rds"))
hm <- function(x) sprintf("%02d:%02d", as.integer(round(x)) %/% 60, as.integer(round(x)) %% 60)
js <- function(p, th, col) { x <- as.data.table(J$str_third); x[[col]][x$place == p & x$third %in% th] }
jsm <- function(tm, y = "overall") { x <- as.data.table(J$school_models); x$b[x$term == tm & x$outcome == y] / x$se[x$term == tm & x$outcome == y] }
sb_city <- as.data.table(J$sbus$by_school)[net == "bh" & oas >= 20]
sbv <- function(n, col) sb_city[[col]][sb_city$name == n]
sb_all <- as.data.table(J$sbus$by_school)[oas >= 20 & !is.na(overall) & !is.na(late)]
cbs <- function(y, col = "b", s = "All schools", tm = "up_back") { x <- as.data.table(CB$sch_models); x[[col]][x$outcome == y & x$sample == s & x$term == tm] }
cbc <- function(y, col = "b", tm = "up_back", ph = "sec", bn = "All tenths") { x <- as.data.table(CB$cell_models); x[[col]][x$outcome == y & x$term == tm & x$phase == ph & x$band == bn] }
cbl <- function(g, ct, col = "b", ph = "sec") { x <- as.data.table(CB$la_models); x[[col]][x$group == g & x$control == ct & x$phase == ph] }
jbus <- J$places |> filter(scenario == "walk_bus"); jwalk <- J$places |> filter(scenario == "walk")
jd <- function(p, k, s = "walk_bus") J$tenths$t[J$tenths$place == p & J$tenths$dec == k & J$tenths$scenario == s]
jc <- function(y, x, s = "All tenths") { z <- J$cell_models; z$b_sd[z$y == y & z$x == x & z$sample == s] }
bh_u <- bh_near - R$bh$med_urban_nl; bh_w <- R$by_band$b[R$by_band$band == "Most deprived three tenths" & R$by_band$phase == "sec"]
# The 109 mostly urban authorities (R/29) and GCSE results (R/30)
JL <- readRDS(here::here("data", "journey_la.rds")); GC <- readRDS(here::here("data", "distance_gcse.rds"))
PL <- JL$places[in_models == TRUE]
ol <- function(m, col = "bh") JL$outlier_all[[col]][JL$outlier_all$measure == m]
gap_top <- PL[order(-t_bus_gap)]
dense <- PL[log_density >= quantile(log_density, 2/3)][order(-t_bus_gap)]
adj_v <- function(y0, sp, n0, col) JL$adj[[col]][JL$adj$y == y0 & JL$adj$spec == sp & JL$adj$n == n0]
lam <- function(term0, g = "dis", s = "All 109", ph = "sec", ctl = "And every control", col = "b") { x <- JL$la_models; x[[col]][x$term == term0 & x$group == g & x$sample == s & x$phase == ph & x$ctrl == ctl & x$outcome == "overall"] }
lat <- function(...) lam(..., col = "b") / lam(..., col = "se")
ha <- function(col, g = "dis", s = "All 109") { x <- JL$horse_a; x[[col]][x$group == g & x$sample == s & x$ctrl == "And every control"] }
lg_t <- function(term0, g = "dis", s = "All 109") { x <- JL$la_given; i <- x$term == term0 & x$group == g & x$sample == s & x$ctrl == "And every control" & x$phase == "sec"; x$b[i] / x$se[i] }
cl_t <- function(term0, ctl, s = "All authorities", ph = "sec", col = "t") { x <- JL$cell_models; i <- x$term == term0 & x$ctrl == ctl & x$sample == s & x$phase == ph & x$outcome == "overall"; if (col == "t") x$b[i] / x$se[i] else x$b[i] * x$sd_x[i] }
bhc <- JL$bh_chg[order(-children)]
gs <- function(mo, col = "b", s = "All schools") { x <- GC$school_models; x[[col]][x$model == mo & x$sample == s] }
gch <- function(g, s, col, ctl = "And every control") { x <- GC$chain; x[[col]][x$group == g & x$sample == s & x$ctrl == ctl] }
AJ <- readRDS(here::here("data", "admissions_journeys.rds"))   # R/31, the city's school system model
aje <- function(m, col, y = 2026) { x <- AJ$effects; x[[col]][x$measure == m & x$year == y] }
aj_run <- function(i, col, y = 2026) { x <- AJ$runs; x[[col]][x$id == i & x$year == y] }
AP <- readRDS(here::here("data", "admissions_proposals.rds"))  # R/32, the proposals run on the published model
apr <- function(i, col, y = 2026) { x <- AP$runs; x[[col]][x$id == i & x$year == y] }
ape <- function(i, col, y = 2026) { x <- AP$effects; x[[col]][x$id == i & x$year == y] }
aps <- function(p, col, cuts = FALSE) { x <- AP$sweep; x[[col]][abs(x$p6 - p) < 1e-9 & x$cuts == cuts] }
AN <- readRDS(here::here("data", "admissions_neighbourhoods.rds"))  # R/33, the same runs by neighbourhood
WH_G <- "Out of Longhill's catchment, into Stringer and Varndean's"
ang <- function(g, col) AN$groups[[col]][AN$groups$group == g]
anw <- function(col) ang(WH_G, col)
ans <- function(ch, col) AN$spread[[col]][AN$spread$change == ch]
anp <- function(ct, col) AN$proposal_groups[[col]][AN$proposal_groups$catchment == ct]
anw_prop <- function(col) { z <- AN$zones[AN$zones$group == WH_G, ]; if (col == "d_dis") sum(z$d_prop_dis * z$dis_today) / sum(z$dis_today) else sum(z$d_prop * z$children_today) / sum(z$children_today) }
source(here::here("R", "route_figs.R"))   # example routes (R/34): RX, the figure functions and map credits
```

::: {.callout-important}
## In short

- **Across England, children in deprived neighbourhoods usually live closer to a secondary school.** That holds in cities, towns and the countryside, and in `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 - fsh)` of districts.
- **Brighton and Hove is the other way round.** Children in the most deprived third of its neighbourhoods live `r km(dv(BH, "near_dep"))` from their nearest school, in a straight line, and the rest live `r km(dv(BH, "near_rest"))`. That is `r pcf(dv(BH, "ratio"))` further, the `r ord(dv(BH, "rank_ratio"))` largest difference of `r nd` districts proportionately and the `r ord(dv(BH, "rank_gap"))` largest in kilometres. Among the `r nrow(ula)` mostly urban local authorities, none has its deprived neighbourhoods further from a school.
- **Absence goes with distance, more for disadvantaged pupils, in every year tested.** Across `r nrow(la)` authorities and six years from 2018/19, disadvantaged pupils' absence is `r sprintf("%.1f", oa("dis", "None beyond share and urbanity", "All authorities"))` points higher for each extra kilometre between deprived neighbourhoods and a school, against `r sprintf("%.1f", oa("non", "None beyond share and urbanity", "All authorities"))` for non-disadvantaged pupils and `r sprintf("%.1f", oa("all", "None beyond share and urbanity", "All authorities"))` for all pupils. It holds on eleven measures of distance and is far weaker in primary schools, as it should be if the journey to secondary school matters.
- **But most of that slope is who lives in those places, not the journey.** Given the ethnic mix of disadvantaged pupils in each authority, the slope falls to `r sprintf("%.1f", gm("dis", "And full ethnic mix of this group"))`, and with every control to `r sprintf("%.1f", gm("dis", "And every control"))`, with an interval that includes zero. Ethnic mix is a confounder here: places with schools close together tend to have disadvantaged pupils from groups who attend more.
- **A smaller link remains in three separate tests.** In mostly urban authorities outside London, the slope for disadvantaged pupils is still `r sprintf("%.1f", gm("dis", "And ethnic mix and region", "Mostly urban, without London"))` points per kilometre given ethnic mix and region, against `r sprintf("%.1f", gp("dis", "Primary, and region"))` in primary schools. Within one authority, pupils in the most deprived neighbourhoods have `r sprintf("%.2f", bw("Most deprived three tenths", "Within, given Census character"))` points more absence per kilometre. And each doubling of how far a school's nearest children live goes with `r sprintf("%.2f", swp("overall", "b1"))` points more absence in every year, given the school's intake and ethnic make-up, and more where more pupils are on free school meals. For disadvantaged pupils the link is mainly with unauthorised and persistent absence, not illness. These are associations, not proof of cause.
- **Moving a school would change this.** A school back on CoMArt's old site, or Longhill moved to the top of Elm Grove, would bring the deprived neighbourhoods of Brighton and Hove to about `r kms(wi("A school", "near_dep"))` to `r kms(wi("Longhill", "near_dep"))` km and close most of the gap.
- **Real journeys tell the same story for Brighton and Hove.** By walking and bus, children in its most deprived neighbourhoods are `r sprintf("%.1f", jt(BH, "gap"))` minutes further from a school than the rest, and walking alone `r sprintf("%.1f", jt(BH, "gap", "walk"))` minutes. No comparator place is more than `r sprintf("%.1f", max(jbus$gap[jbus$place != BH]))` minutes further by walking and bus, and its deprived neighbourhoods need the most changes of bus. See [journey times](#sec-journeys).
- **Among all `r nrow(PL)` mostly urban authorities, none has its deprived neighbourhoods as far from a school by walking and bus.** The next largest gaps are `r and_list(sprintf("%s (%.1f minutes)", gap_top$la[2:3], gap_top$t_bus_gap[2:3]))`, and in the median authority the deprived third is nearer. It is mostly distance, not slow buses, but `r sprintf("%.0f%%", ol("p_two_dep"))` of those journeys need two or more buses, the most of any authority. See [the 109 authorities](#sec-la-journeys).
- **Across those authorities, distance still goes with disadvantaged absence, and the rest of the journey adds little.** With every control, `r sprintf("%.1f", lam("km1_dep"))` points per kilometre (`r sprintf("%.1f", lam("km1_dep", s = "Without London"))` outside London), and little in primary. Journey time does not beat straight-line distance, and changes of bus, waiting and missing a bus add nothing once distance is known. The climb on the walk home, and busy change points (mostly in London), are hints that need more testing. School buses show no general link either: Longhill, where missing the last workable journey means arriving about `r sprintf("%.0f", sbv("Longhill High School", "late"))` minutes late, is a striking case, not a pattern.
- **What it could mean for GCSE results.** *If* the extra absence is caused by the journey, each kilometre would cost disadvantaged pupils about `r sprintf("%.1f", -gch("dis", "All 109", "chain_va"))` to `r sprintf("%.1f", -gch("dis", "Without London", "chain_va"))` Attainment 8 points, and Brighton and Hove's gap about `r sprintf("%.0f", -GC$bh$km_gap * gch("dis", "Without London", "chain_va"))`. That is about the lower end of Gorard and Siddiqui's estimate of what mixing intakes could gain, `r sprintf("%.0f", GC$gorard$att8[["lo"]])` to `r sprintf("%.0f", GC$gorard$att8[["hi"]])` points. GCSE results do not show the distance cost directly. See [GCSE results](#sec-gcse).
- **The admissions changes themselves did little either way.** On the city's school system model, the 2024 map and priority 6 together lengthened disadvantaged children's journeys by about `r sprintf("%.1f", aje("dep_min", "both"))` minutes and lowered segregation by about `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * AJ$summary[change == "both", share_removed])`. In Attainment 8 points that is a journey cost of about `r sprintf("%.2f", -AJ$summary[change == "both", cost_lo])` against a generous mixing gain of up to `r sprintf("%.2f", AJ$summary[change == "both", gain_hi])`: both a fraction of a point. The gap comes from where the schools are. The council's first proposal, priority 6 at 20% with Dorothy Stringer and Blatchington Mill cut to 300, would have lengthened journeys a little more and displaced more children, for no gain in mixing, and Class Divide's 30%, with the same cuts, would have done no more. See [the admissions changes](#sec-admissions) and [the proposals](#sec-proposals).
- **But the city average hides Whitehawk.** The 2024 map moved about `r sprintf("%.0f", anw("children"))` children a year in Whitehawk out of Longhill's catchment, and lengthened their journeys, already among the city's longest, by `r sprintf("%.1f", anw("d_all"))` minutes, and by `r sprintf("%.1f", anw("d_dis"))` for the disadvantaged children among them. On the chain that is up to about `r sprintf("%.1f", -AN$whitehawk_cost[1])` Attainment 8 points each. See [whose journeys changed](#sec-admissions-neighbourhoods).
- **Most of this page is in straight lines.** They ignore hills, bus routes and catchments, and a child's nearest school need not be the one they attend. Every source and calculation is in [the methodology](method.qmd#sec-distance-method).
:::

## What this measures {#sec-measure}

How far each school's own pupils travel is not published, so this page starts from where children live and where schools are. This is a summary: [the methodology](method.qmd#sec-distance-method) gives every source, vintage and formula.

- **Schools.** Every open state-funded secondary, all-through and middle deemed secondary school in England in the DfE's register, Get Information About Schools (`r D$gias_date`): `r format(D$n_schools, big.mark = ",")` schools taking pupils at 13 or younger and keeping them to at least 16. Special schools, pupil referral units and independent schools are left out.
- **Neighbourhoods.** England's `r format(D$n_lsoa, big.mark = ",")` Census 2021 Lower Layer Super Output Areas, each placed at the mean of its Output Areas' population-weighted centroids. Averages are weighted by the 10 to 14 year olds living there.
- **Deprivation.** The share of households deprived in two or more of the Census's four dimensions (employment, education, health, housing), the same measure as [the neighbourhood covariates](neighbourhood_covariates.qmd).
- **Distance.** The straight line to the nearest school. Each place's neighbourhoods are split into its most deprived third and the rest, so the comparison is always within one place.
- **Kind of place.** The ONS 2021 rural-urban classification. A district or authority is "mostly urban" if at least 80% of its 10 to 14 year olds live in urban neighbourhoods.

Schools in Wales are not in the register used here, so a few neighbourhoods on the border look further from a school than they are.

## Across England, deprived neighbourhoods are nearer {#sec-england}

Within each kind of place, the most deprived neighbourhoods tend to be among the closest to a school. One likely reason is that they are usually denser and more central.

```{r}
#| label: fig-national
#| fig-cap: "Mean straight-line distance from home to the nearest state secondary school, by how deprived the neighbourhood is (England's tenths, 10 = most deprived) and the ONS 2021 rural-urban class of the neighbourhood. Weighted by 10 to 14 year olds."
#| fig-height: 4.4
n <- D$national |> mutate(kind3 = factor(kind3, c(RU, UF, UR)))
ends <- n |> filter(dep_dec == 10)
ggplot(n, aes(dep_dec, near, colour = kind3)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) + geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  geom_text(data = ends, aes(label = kms(near)), hjust = -0.35, size = 3.3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = PLACE_COL, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10, expand = expansion(mult = c(0.03, 0.08))) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(x = "Neighbourhood deprivation (10 = most deprived tenth of England)", y = "Distance to nearest school (km)") +
  theme_note()
```

Taken across England as a whole, children in the most deprived third of neighbourhoods live `r km(D$england$near_dep)` from a school and the rest `r km(D$england$near_rest)`. Much of that is town against country, which is why the rest of this page compares neighbourhoods within one place.

## Where it runs the other way {#sec-districts}

In `r sprintf("%.0f%%", fsh)` of England's `r nd` districts, children in the most deprived third of neighbourhoods live further from a school than the rest. Among the `r nu` mostly urban districts it is `r sprintf("%.0f%%", fshu)`. Brighton and Hove is near the top of both lists.

```{r}
#| label: fig-districts
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("How much further children in the most deprived third of neighbourhoods live from their nearest school than children in the rest of the same district, for all ", nd, " districts, from largest to smallest. Above 1, the deprived neighbourhoods are further away.")
#| fig-height: 4.6
sh <- c(BH, "Hastings", "Blackpool", "Southampton", "Portsmouth", "Plymouth", "Bristol", "Newham", "Tower Hamlets")
dp <- dd |> arrange(desc(ratio)) |> mutate(pos = row_number(), hi = place %in% sh,
       col = case_when(place == BH ~ "Brighton and Hove", hi ~ "Places on this page", TRUE ~ "Other districts"))
ggplot(dp, aes(pos, ratio)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = GREY, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(data = filter(dp, !hi), colour = LIGHT, size = 1.6) +
  geom_point(data = filter(dp, hi), aes(colour = col), size = 2.8) +
  geom_text_repel(data = filter(dp, hi), aes(label = place), size = 3.2, colour = INK, min.segment.length = 0, box.padding = 0.4, seed = 4, max.overlaps = 30) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Brighton and Hove" = BPURPLE, "Places on this page" = DPURPLE), name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0.4, 1.6, 0.2)) +
  labs(x = paste0("District, from largest difference to smallest (", nd, " districts)"), y = "Most deprived third ÷ other neighbourhoods") +
  theme_note()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-top
#| tbl-cap: "The districts where children in deprived neighbourhoods live furthest from a school, relative to the rest of the district, with the rank in kilometres. Straight-line distance to the nearest school, in kilometres."
dd |> arrange(rank_ratio) |> slice_head(n = 10) |>
  transmute(Rank = rank_ratio, District = place, `Most deprived third` = kms(near_dep), `Other neighbourhoods` = kms(near_rest),
            `Difference (km)` = sprintf("%+.2f", gap), `Rank in km` = rank_gap, `Kind of place` = kind) |>
  kt(align = "rlrrrrl")
```

The list mixes outer London boroughs, commuter towns and cities such as Derby. Here is Brighton and Hove against other coastal and urban places, and against the rest of Sussex:

```{r}
#| label: fig-compare
#| fig-cap: "Straight-line distance to the nearest school: children in the most deprived third of each place's neighbourhoods against children in the rest."
#| fig-height: 4.8
cp <- bind_rows(D$compare, D$sussex |> filter(!place %in% D$compare$place)) |> arrange(ratio) |> mutate(place = factor(place, place))
cl <- cp |> select(place, near_dep, near_rest) |> pivot_longer(-place) |>
  mutate(name = recode(name, near_dep = "Most deprived third", near_rest = "Other neighbourhoods"))
ggplot(cp, aes(y = place)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = near_dep, xend = near_rest, yend = place), colour = LIGHT, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = cl, aes(x = value, colour = name), size = 2.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = THIRD_COL, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(x = "Distance to nearest school (km)", y = NULL) + theme_note() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(face = ifelse(levels(cp$place) == BH, "bold", "plain")))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-compare
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Places compared. Distance to the nearest school in kilometres for the most deprived third of neighbourhoods and the rest, how much further that is, with the rank of ", nd, " districts in brackets, the share of secondary pupils who are disadvantaged, and absence in state-funded secondary schools, full year 2024/25, for disadvantaged pupils, non-disadvantaged pupils and all pupils (DfE, absence by pupil characteristics). DfE publishes these by authority, not by district, so Hastings has none.")
na_dash <- function(x, f) ifelse(is.na(x), "–", sprintf(f, x))
D$compare |> arrange(desc(ratio)) |>
  transmute(Place = place, `Deprived third` = kms(near_dep), Other = kms(near_rest),
            Further = paste0(sprintf("%+.0f%%", 100 * (ratio - 1)), " (", rank_ratio, ")"),
            Share = na_dash(share, "%.0f%%"),
            `Disadv.` = na_dash(abs_dis, "%.1f%%"), `Non-disadv.` = na_dash(abs_non, "%.1f%%"), All = na_dash(abs_all, "%.1f%%")) |>
  kt(align = "lrrrrrrr") |>
  kableExtra::add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Distance to school" = 3, "Pupils disadv." = 1, "Absence" = 3))
```

### Brighton and Hove and Hastings on the map {#sec-maps}

```{r}
#| label: fig-dots
#| fig-cap: "Each dot is a neighbourhood, sized by its 10 to 14 year olds and shaded by the straight-line distance to its nearest secondary school. A ring marks the most deprived third of the place's neighbourhoods. Diamonds are state secondary schools. Census 2021 and Get Information About Schools."
#| fig-height: 8.2
dot_map <- function(p, lab = FALSE) {
  z <- D$dots |> filter(lad == p)
  sc <- D$dot_schools |> filter(e > min(z$x) - 1500, e < max(z$x) + 1500, n > min(z$y) - 1500, n < max(z$y) + 1500) |>
    mutate(short = sub(" Academy Hastings$", " Hastings", name), short = sub(" Academy St Leonards$", " St Leonards", short),
           short = sub(" (Catholic |Community |High )?(School|College|Academy).*$", "", short),
           short = recode(short, "Brighton Aldridge" = "BACA", "Portslade Aldridge" = "PACA"))
  ggplot(z, aes(x, y)) +
    geom_point(aes(size = kids, colour = near1)) +
    geom_point(data = filter(z, dep_third), aes(size = kids), shape = 21, colour = INK, fill = NA, stroke = 1, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_point(data = sc, aes(e, n), shape = 23, size = 3, fill = BLUE, colour = "white", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    geom_text_repel(data = sc, aes(e, n, label = short), size = 2.8, colour = INK, seed = 7, inherit.aes = FALSE, min.segment.length = 0, max.overlaps = 40) +
    scale_colour_gradient(low = PPURPLE, high = DPURPLE, name = "km to nearest school", limits = c(0, 3), oob = scales::squish) +
    scale_size_area(max_size = 4, guide = "none") + coord_equal() +
    labs(title = p, x = NULL, y = NULL) + theme_note() +
    theme(axis.text = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank())
}
(dot_map(BH) / dot_map("Hastings")) + plot_layout(guides = "collect") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

In Brighton and Hove, the neighbourhoods furthest from a school are in the east of the city, around Whitehawk, between the central schools and Longhill. The [city's school system](https://adamdennett.github.io/bh-school-system/analysis.html) model finds the same in routed walk and bus times: in its [simulator](https://adamdennett-bh-school-system.share.connect.posit.cloud/), disadvantaged children travel about 4 minutes further each way than everyone else.

### Does it depend on how it is measured? {#sec-checks}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-checks
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("How much further the most deprived third of neighbourhoods is from a school than the rest, on five versions of the measure, with each place's rank of ", nd, " districts.")
D$checks |> mutate(v = paste0(sprintf("%+.0f%%", 100 * (ratio - 1)), " (", rank, ")")) |>
  select(Measure = spec, lad, v) |> pivot_wider(names_from = lad, values_from = v) |>
  select(Measure, all_of(c(BH, "Hastings", "Blackpool"))) |> kt(align = "lrrr")
```

Brighton and Hove's result holds on every version: its deprived neighbourhoods are `r pcf(min(D$checks$ratio[D$checks$lad == BH]))` to `r pcf(max(D$checks$ratio[D$checks$lad == BH]))` further, in the top `r max(D$checks$rank[D$checks$lad == BH])` of `r nd` districts. Hastings and Blackpool are less certain. Their deprived neighbourhoods are further from their nearest school, but the difference is much smaller on the mean of the three nearest (`r sprintf("%+.0f%%", 100 * (ck("Mean of the three nearest", "Hastings", "ratio") - 1))` and `r sprintf("%+.0f%%", 100 * (ck("Mean of the three nearest", "Blackpool", "ratio") - 1))`). In Hastings it reverses (`r sprintf("%+.0f%%", 100 * (ck("Nearest neither selective nor faith", "Hastings", "ratio") - 1))`) if faith and selective schools are set aside.

## Does absence go with distance? {#sec-absence}

[FFT Education Datalab](https://ffteducationdatalab.org.uk/2023/11/are-pupils-who-live-further-away-from-their-school-absent-more-often/) compared pupils within schools, using straight-line distance from their home postcodes. Those living furthest away were absent slightly more often, and the difference was wider for disadvantaged pupils. FFT calls distance "a relatively minor factor" and suggests that travel times may be instructive. Published data allow several further tests. Every source and calculation is set out in [the methodology](method.qmd#sec-distance-method).

### A first look: by authority, for all three groups {#sec-la}

DfE publishes absence by disadvantage for each local authority, so the distance from deprived neighbourhoods to a school can be set against absence for each group of pupils.

```{r}
#| label: fig-absence
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Absence in state-funded secondary schools, 2024/25, against the straight-line distance to a school from the most deprived third of each local authority's neighbourhoods, for ", nrow(la), " authorities. Lines are simple fits.")
#| fig-height: 4.6
lp <- la |> select(place, near_dep, london, Disadvantaged = abs_dis, `Non-disadvantaged` = abs_non, `All pupils` = abs_all) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Disadvantaged, `Non-disadvantaged`, `All pupils`), names_to = "group", values_to = "abs") |>
  mutate(group = factor(group, c("All pupils", "Disadvantaged", "Non-disadvantaged")),
         who = case_when(place == BH ~ "Brighton and Hove", london ~ "London", TRUE ~ "Elsewhere"))
ggplot(lp, aes(near_dep, abs)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, colour = GREY, linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(data = filter(lp, who != "Brighton and Hove"), aes(colour = who), size = 1.7, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = filter(lp, who == "Brighton and Hove"), aes(colour = who), size = 3.4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Brighton and Hove" = BPURPLE, "London" = BLUE, "Elsewhere" = LIGHT), name = NULL) +
  facet_wrap(~group) +
  labs(x = "Distance to nearest school, most deprived third of neighbourhoods (km)", y = "Absence, % of sessions") + theme_note()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-la-ci
#| fig-cap: !expr paste("Points of absence for each extra kilometre between an authority's most deprived neighbourhoods and a school, 2024/25, the estimates in the table below.", CI_NOTE)
#| fig-height: 3
D$la_models |> transmute(row = spec, group, b, se) |> ci_plot("Points of absence per km")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-la
#| tbl-cap: "Points of absence for each extra kilometre between an authority's most deprived neighbourhoods and a school, 2024/25, for each group of pupils, with 95% intervals. Second and third rows allow for the share of pupils who are disadvantaged and how urban the authority is."
D$la_models |> mutate(v = sprintf("%+.1f (%+.1f to %+.1f)", b, b - 1.96 * se, b + 1.96 * se),
                      spec = paste0(spec, " (", n, " authorities)")) |>
  select(spec, group, v) |> pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = v) |>
  select(`Specification` = spec, `All pupils`, Disadvantaged, `Non-disadvantaged`) |> kt(align = "lrrr")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## The model behind this table

$$\text{absence}_a = \alpha + \beta\,\text{near\_dep}_a + \gamma_1\,\text{share}_a + \gamma_2\,\text{urban\_share}_a + \varepsilon_a$$

```r
# R/18_distance.R: one row per authority, 2024/25; the same for abs_non and abs_all
lm(abs_dis ~ near_dep,                       data = la)                 # Distance alone
lm(abs_dis ~ near_dep + share + urban_share, data = la)                 # Given share and urbanity
lm(abs_dis ~ near_dep + share + urban_share, data = filter(la, !london))  # And without London
```

$\beta$ is the table's figure: points of absence for each extra kilometre. `abs_dis`, `abs_non`, `abs_all` are overall absence, % of sessions, in state-funded secondary schools for each group; `near_dep` is the child-weighted mean straight-line km from the authority's most deprived third of neighbourhoods to the nearest state secondary; `share` is the % of pupils disadvantaged; `urban_share` the % of 10 to 14 year olds in urban neighbourhoods.
:::

The slope looks about `r round(lm_b("Disadvantaged", S1) / lm_b("Non-disadvantaged", S1))` times steeper for disadvantaged pupils than for non-disadvantaged pupils once share and urbanity are allowed for, and about `r round(lm_b("Disadvantaged", S2) / lm_b("Non-disadvantaged", S2))` times steeper without London. London pulls the fit up, because its schools are close together and its disadvantaged pupils attend well.

It is the distance that goes with absence, not the gap within the authority. Added to the same model, how much further the deprived neighbourhoods are than the rest has no clear relationship with absence for any group (`r paste(sprintf("%s t = %.1f", tolower(D$la_ratio_models$group), D$la_ratio_models$t), collapse = ", ")`). Fairness in access and the level of access are separate questions.

One year, one measure and three controls cannot carry much weight. The rest of this section tries to break the result.

### How firm is it? {#sec-firm}

::: {.callout-note}
## The answer so far

**The pattern is consistent. The size of @fig-absence is not to be trusted.** Absence goes with distance in every year from 2018/19 and on every measure of distance tried, more for disadvantaged pupils, and far less in primary schools. But most of the slope in @fig-absence comes from who lives where. Given the ethnic mix of each group of pupils it falls by about four-fifths, and with every control no clear slope is left across all authorities. A smaller link remains in mostly urban authorities, within authorities for the most deprived neighbourhoods, and between schools.
:::

@tbl-ladder puts the authority tests side by side, pooling the six years.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ladder-ci
#| fig-cap: !expr paste("The tests in the table below, in points of absence per kilometre.", CI_NOTE)
#| fig-height: 8
lad3 <- function(lab, f) bind_rows(lapply(c("all", "dis", "non"), function(g) tibble(row = lab, group = unname(GRL[g]), b = f(g, "b"), se = f(g, "se"))))
bind_rows(
  lad3("Secondary, all authorities", function(g, k) oa(g, "None beyond share and urbanity", "All authorities", k)),
  lad3("Secondary, without London", function(g, k) oa(g, "None beyond share and urbanity", "Without London", k)),
  lad3("Secondary, given region", function(g, k) oa(g, "Region", "All authorities", k)),
  lad3("Secondary, given the group's ethnic mix", function(g, k) gm(g, "And full ethnic mix of this group", col = k)),
  lad3("Secondary, given every control", function(g, k) gm(g, "And every control", col = k)),
  lad3("Mostly urban, without London", function(g, k) oa(g, "None beyond share and urbanity", "Mostly urban, without London", k)),
  lad3("Mostly urban, without London, given ethnic mix", function(g, k) gm(g, "And full ethnic mix of this group", "Mostly urban, without London", k)),
  lad3("Mostly urban, without London, given ethnic mix and region", function(g, k) gm(g, "And ethnic mix and region", "Mostly urban, without London", k)),
  lad3("Mostly urban, without London, given every control", function(g, k) gm(g, "And every control", "Mostly urban, without London", k)),
  lad3("Less urban authorities", function(g, k) { x <- R$urb_sample |> filter(group == g, sample == "Less urban", control == "Share, urban"); x[[k]] }),
  lad3("Falsification: primary absence", function(g, k) pl(paste0(g, "_pri"), col = k)),
  lad3("Secondary minus primary absence", function(g, k) pl(paste0("step_", g), col = k)),
  lad3("Authority effects, as networks changed", function(g, k) { x <- R$fe_la |> filter(out == paste0(g, "_sec")); x[[k]] })) |>
  ci_plot("Points of absence per km")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ladder
#| tbl-cap: "Points of absence for each extra kilometre between an authority's most deprived neighbourhoods and a school, for each group of pupils, with 95% intervals. All years pooled: 2018/19 and 2020/21 to 2024/25, with year effects and errors clustered by authority. Every row allows for the share of pupils who are disadvantaged and how urban the authority is, except the authority-effects row, which allows for the share."
ladder <- function(lab, f) { tibble(Test = lab, `All pupils` = f("all"), Disadvantaged = f("dis"), `Non-disadvantaged` = f("non")) }
key <- function(g, stem = "sec") paste0(g, "_", stem)
LAD <- bind_rows(
  ladder("Secondary, all authorities", function(g) oa_ci(g, "None beyond share and urbanity", "All authorities")),
  ladder("... without London", function(g) oa_ci(g, "None beyond share and urbanity", "Without London")),
  ladder("... given region", function(g) oa_ci(g, "Region", "All authorities")),
  ladder("... given the ethnic mix of that group", function(g) gm_ci(g, "And full ethnic mix of this group")),
  ladder("... given every control", function(g) gm_ci(g, "And every control")),
  ladder("Mostly urban, without London", function(g) oa_ci(g, "None beyond share and urbanity", "Mostly urban, without London")),
  ladder("... given the ethnic mix of that group", function(g) gm_ci(g, "And full ethnic mix of this group", "Mostly urban, without London")),
  ladder("... given ethnic mix and region", function(g) gm_ci(g, "And ethnic mix and region", "Mostly urban, without London")),
  ladder("... given every control", function(g) gm_ci(g, "And every control", "Mostly urban, without London")),
  ladder("Less urban authorities", function(g) { x <- R$urb_sample |> filter(group == g, sample == "Less urban", control == "Share, urban"); ci2(x$b, x$se) }),
  ladder("Falsification: primary absence", function(g) pl_ci(key(g, "pri"))),
  ladder("Secondary minus primary absence", function(g) pl_ci(paste0("step_", g))),
  ladder("Authority effects: as each school network changed", function(g) { x <- R$fe_la |> filter(out == key(g)); ci2(x$b, x$se) }))
LAD |> kt(align = "lrrr")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## The model behind this table

$$\text{absence}_{a,t} = \beta\,\text{near\_dep}_{a,t} + \gamma_1\,\text{share}_{a,t} + \gamma_2\,\text{urban\_share}_{a} + \boldsymbol{\delta}'\mathbf{x}_{a,t} + \tau_t + \varepsilon_{a,t}$$

```r
# R/19_distance_absence.R: authorities by year, secondary, one group at a time
feols(overall ~ near_dep + share + urban_share | tp, data = A, cluster = ~la)                   # first rows
feols(overall ~ near_dep + share + urban_share + gor_name | tp, ...)                             # given region
feols(overall ~ near_dep + share + urban_share + eth_wb + eth_asian + eth_black + eth_mixed | tp, ...)   # given ethnic mix
feols(overall ~ near_dep + share + urban_share + eth_wb + eth_asian + eth_black + eth_mixed + gor_name +
        graduates + bad_health + white_british + social_rent + no_car + deprived + log_density +
        sen_sup + ehcp + ks2_c + eal + wbri + mobile | tp, ...)                                  # every control
```

$t$ is the year (2018/19, 2020/21 to 2024/25), $\tau_t$ year effects, and errors are clustered by authority $a$. $\mathbf{x}$ is whichever extra controls the row names. The primary rows use primary absence on the left. Every variable is in [the glossary](method.qmd#sec-model-variables).
:::

#### Across six years {#sec-years}

```{r}
#| label: fig-years
#| fig-cap: "Points of absence for each extra kilometre between an authority's most deprived neighbourhoods and a school, year by year, using the school network of that September, with 95% intervals and allowing for the share disadvantaged and how urban the authority is. DfE publishes no 2019/20. Full years, state-funded secondary schools."
#| fig-height: 6
yy <- bind_rows(R$by_year |> filter(control == "Share disadvantaged, how urban") |> select(group, tp, sample, b, se), R$urban_year |> select(group, tp, sample, b, se)) |>
  filter(sample %in% c("All authorities", "Without London", "Mostly urban, without London", "Less urban")) |>
  mutate(group = factor(unname(GRL[group]), names(GROUP_COL)[1:3]), year = factor(ylab(tp), ylab(sort(unique(tp)))),
         sample = factor(sample, c("All authorities", "Without London", "Mostly urban, without London", "Less urban")))
ggplot(yy, aes(year, b, colour = group)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GREY, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = b - 1.96 * se, ymax = b + 1.96 * se), position = position_dodge(width = 0.55), size = 0.3, linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = GROUP_COL, name = NULL) + facet_wrap(~sample, ncol = 2) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Points of absence per km") + theme_note() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1))
```

The slope for disadvantaged pupils is positive in all six years, from `r sprintf("%.1f", min(yd$b))` to `r sprintf("%.1f", max(yd$b))` points per kilometre. It was already there before the pandemic (`r sprintf("%+.1f", yd$b[yd$tp == 201819])` in 2018/19) and has been larger since 2021/22. Authorities whose deprived neighbourhoods were further from a school saw disadvantaged absence rise more between 2018/19 and 2024/25 (`r sprintf("%+.1f", R$rise$b[R$rise$group == "dis"])` points per kilometre, t = `r sprintf("%.1f", R$rise$b[R$rise$group == "dis"] / R$rise$se[R$rise$group == "dis"])`), with no clear difference for non-disadvantaged pupils (`r sprintf("%+.1f", R$rise$b[R$rise$group == "non"])`, t = `r sprintf("%.1f", R$rise$b[R$rise$group == "non"] / R$rise$se[R$rise$group == "non"])`).

Distance is recalculated each year from school opening and closing dates, so earlier years are not measured against today's schools. The network has grown from `r format(R$network_n$schools[1], big.mark = ",")` schools in September 2018 to `r format(R$network_n$schools[nrow(R$network_n)], big.mark = ",")` in September 2025.

#### On every measure of distance, and in every model {#sec-curve}

To avoid resting on any one choice, the same model was fitted on every combination of `r length(unique(R$curve$tp))` years, `r length(R$measures)` measures of distance, `r length(R$controls)` sets of controls and `r length(R$samples)` samples of authorities, for each group of pupils: `r format(sum(cv_sec$group == "dis"), big.mark = ",")` models per group, shown in @fig-curve. These models are not independent of one another, so the shares describe how far the answer depends on the choices made. They are not a significance test.

```{r}
#| label: fig-curve
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("A specification curve of ", format(nrow(cv_sec), big.mark = ","), " models of secondary absence, each dot one model, sorted by size, in points of absence for one standard deviation more distance. Purple dots have a 95% interval wholly above zero, blue dots wholly below, grey dots include zero.")
#| fig-height: 3.8
cz <- cv_sec |> mutate(group = factor(unname(GRL[group]), names(GROUP_COL)[1:3]), clear = case_when(t > 1.96 ~ "Clearly above zero", t < -1.96 ~ "Clearly below zero", TRUE ~ "Interval includes zero")) |>
  group_by(group) |> arrange(b_sd, .by_group = TRUE) |> mutate(pos = 100 * (row_number() - 0.5) / n()) |> ungroup()
ggplot(cz, aes(pos, b_sd, colour = clear)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GREY, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(size = 0.7) + facet_wrap(~group) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Clearly above zero" = BPURPLE, "Clearly below zero" = BLUE, "Interval includes zero" = LIGHT), name = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2.5))) +
  labs(x = "Models, from smallest to largest (%)", y = "Points of absence per SD of distance") + theme_note()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-curve
#| tbl-cap: "The share of those models in which the slope is above zero, and in brackets the share in which its 95% interval is wholly above zero, by the set of controls and the sample of authorities."
cshare <- function(col) cv_sec |> mutate(k = .data[[col]]) |> group_by(k, group) |>
  summarise(v = sprintf("%.0f%% (%.0f%%)", 100 * mean(b > 0), 100 * mean(t > 1.96)), .groups = "drop") |> pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = v)
bind_rows(cshare("control") |> mutate(ord = match(k, R$controls), kind = "Controls"), cshare("sample") |> mutate(ord = 100 + match(k, R$samples), kind = "Sample")) |>
  arrange(ord) |> transmute(`Choice` = k, `All pupils` = all, Disadvantaged = dis, `Non-disadvantaged` = non) |> kt(align = "lrrr")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## The model behind this table

$$\text{absence}_a = \alpha + \beta\,\text{distance}^{(m)}_a + \boldsymbol{\gamma}'\mathbf{x}^{(c)}_a + \varepsilon_a \quad \text{(one year at a time)}$$

```r
# R/19_distance_absence.R: every combination of year, distance measure m, control set c and sample
lm(overall ~ measure + <controls>, data = <one year, one sample>)      # HC3 errors
#   measure:  each of the eleven distance measures (table below)
#   controls: none; share and urbanity; and region; and Census place; and pupils; and primary absence
#   sample:   all authorities, without London, mostly urban, mostly urban without London, less urban
```

The table counts how often $\beta > 0$ across those models, and how often its 95% interval is wholly above zero; the figure shows $\beta$ times the standard deviation of the measure that year.
:::

Across all of these, `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(cv_dis$b > 0))` of the slopes for disadvantaged pupils are above zero, `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(cv_dis$t > 1.96))` clearly so and `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(cv_dis$t < -1.96))` clearly below. The choice of measure makes little difference. The choice of controls and sample makes a great deal, as @tbl-curve shows: with few controls most models are clearly positive, and under the fullest sets few are.

```{r}
#| label: fig-measures-ci
#| fig-cap: !expr paste("Points of absence for one standard deviation more of each measure of distance, the estimates in the table below.", CI_NOTE)
#| fig-height: 6.5
R$measure_simple |> filter(sample %in% c("All authorities", "Mostly urban, without London")) |>
  transmute(row = label, group = unname(GRL[group]), b = b_sd, se = se_sd, panel = sample) |> ci_plot("Points of absence per standard deviation of distance", wrap = 40)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-measures
#| tbl-cap: "Eleven measures of distance from an authority's deprived neighbourhoods. Points of absence for one standard deviation more distance, all years pooled, allowing for the share disadvantaged and how urban the authority is. A dagger marks a 95% interval that includes zero."
ms <- R$measure_simple |> filter(sample %in% c("All authorities", "Mostly urban, without London")) |>
  mutate(v = paste0(sprintf("%+.2f", b_sd), ifelse(abs(b_sd / se_sd) < 1.96, "†", "")), col = paste(sample, group)) |>
  select(Measure = label, col, v) |> pivot_wider(names_from = col, values_from = v)
ms |> select(Measure, `All authorities all`, `All authorities dis`, `All authorities non`, `Mostly urban, without London all`, `Mostly urban, without London dis`, `Mostly urban, without London non`) |>
  setNames(c("Measure", "All", "Disadv.", "Non-disadv.", "All ", "Disadv. ", "Non-disadv. ")) |> kt(align = "lrrrrrr") |>
  kableExtra::add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "All authorities" = 3, "Mostly urban, without London" = 3))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## The model behind this table

$$\text{absence}_{a,t} = \beta\,z^{(m)}_{a,t} + \gamma_1\,\text{share}_{a,t} + \gamma_2\,\text{urban\_share}_{a} + \tau_t + \varepsilon_{a,t}, \qquad z^{(m)}_{a,t} = \frac{\text{measure}^{(m)}_{a,t}}{\text{sd}_t\!\left(\text{measure}^{(m)}\right)}$$

```r
# R/19_distance_absence.R: one model for each measure m
feols(overall ~ z + share + urban_share | tp, data = A, cluster = ~la)
```

Each measure is divided by its standard deviation across authorities in that year, so $\beta$ is points of absence for one standard deviation more distance, comparable across measures.
:::

Nor does it depend on a handful of places. @tbl-influence repeats the 2024/25 model with errors that allow for neighbouring authorities being alike, with pupil weights, with a method that discounts outliers, and without the most influential authorities. Dropping any one authority leaves the slope for disadvantaged pupils between `r sprintf("%.1f", ckla("dis", "Baseline, 2024/25 (robust errors)", "loo_min"))` and `r sprintf("%.1f", ckla("dis", "Baseline, 2024/25 (robust errors)", "loo_max"))`.

```{r}
#| label: fig-influence-ci
#| fig-cap: !expr paste("The checks in the table below, in points of absence per kilometre, 2024/25.", CI_NOTE)
#| fig-height: 4
R$checks_la |> transmute(row = check, group = unname(GRL[group]), b, se) |> ci_plot("Points of absence per km")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-influence
#| tbl-cap: "Checks on the 2024/25 model of @tbl-la, given share and urbanity, in points of absence per kilometre with 95% intervals."
R$checks_la |> mutate(v = ci2(b, se)) |> select(Check = check, group, v) |> pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = v) |>
  transmute(Check, `All pupils` = all, Disadvantaged = dis, `Non-disadvantaged` = non) |> kt(align = "lrrr")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## The model behind this table

$$\text{absence}_a = \alpha + \beta\,\text{near\_dep}_a + \gamma_1\,\text{share}_a + \gamma_2\,\text{urban\_share}_a + \varepsilon_a$$

```r
# R/19_distance_absence.R: 2024/25, one row per authority
f <- overall ~ near_dep + share + urban_share
lm(f, d)                                        # the base model
lm(f, d[-i, ])                                  # leaving out each authority in turn
MASS::rlm(f, data = d, method = "MM")           # robust to outliers
lm(f, d, weights = n_all)                       # weighted by pupils, HC3 errors
feols(f, d, vcov = vcov_conley(lat = ~lat, lon = ~lon, cutoff = 100))   # errors allowing for neighbours within 100 km
```
:::

Which neighbourhoods' distance matters is also informative. Put the deprived neighbourhoods and the others in one model, and for disadvantaged pupils the deprived neighbourhoods' distance carries about twice the weight (`r sprintf("%+.1f", rc("dis", "b_dep"))` against `r sprintf("%+.1f", rc("dis", "b_rest"))` per kilometre). For non-disadvantaged pupils the two are about equal (`r sprintf("%+.1f", rc("non", "b_dep"))` and `r sprintf("%+.1f", rc("non", "b_rest"))`).

The relationship is not a straight line, either. Compared with authorities under 1 km, disadvantaged absence is `r sprintf("%.1f", shape_b("dis", "1 to 1.5 km"))` points higher at 1 to 1.5 km and `r sprintf("%.1f", shape_b("dis", "1.5 to 2 km"))` at 1.5 to 2 km, but only `r sprintf("%.1f", shape_b("dis", "2 to 3 km"))` at 2 to 3 km, where there are just `r R$shape$las[R$shape$group == "dis" & R$shape$band == "2 to 3 km"]` authorities, all large and rural.

#### What takes the slope away? {#sec-controls}

Controls overlap, so adding them one by one cannot say which one matters. @fig-gelbach splits the fall from the first model to the fullest into a part for each block of controls, using a method that does not depend on the order they go in (a Gelbach decomposition; [details](method.qmd#sec-distance-models)).

```{r}
#| label: fig-gelbach
#| fig-cap: "How much of the fall in the slope, from the model with share and urbanity to the model with every control, each block of controls accounts for, in points of absence per kilometre, all years pooled, with 95% bootstrap intervals. The parts add up to the whole fall. Below zero, a block would make the slope larger if taken away."
#| fig-height: 5.4
BLOCK_LAB <- c("Ethnic mix of the group, the school population and residents" = "Ethnic mix and language", "Region" = "Region", "Population density" = "Population density", "Health" = "Bad health",
               "Graduates, deprivation, renting, cars" = "Graduates, deprivation, renting, cars", "Pupils' needs, prior attainment, mobility" = "Needs, prior attainment, mobility")
gz <- R$gel_tab |> filter(!term %in% c("base", "full")) |> mutate(group = factor(unname(GRL[group]), rev(names(GROUP_COL)[1:3])), term = factor(unname(BLOCK_LAB[term]), rev(unname(BLOCK_LAB))),
                                                                  sample = factor(sample, c("All authorities", "Without London", "Mostly urban, without London")))
ggplot(gz, aes(est, term, colour = group)) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = GREY, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = est - 1.96 * se, xmax = est + 1.96 * se), position = position_dodge(width = 0.65), size = 0.25, linewidth = 0.55) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = GROUP_COL, breaks = names(GROUP_COL)[1:3], name = NULL) + facet_wrap(~sample, ncol = 3) +
  labs(x = "Part of the fall in the slope (points per km)", y = NULL) + theme_note()
```

**It is ethnic mix, and very little else.** Of the fall from `r sprintf("%.2f", gl("dis", "base"))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", gl("dis", "full"))` points per kilometre for disadvantaged pupils, ethnic mix and language account for `r sprintf("%.2f", gl("dis", gterm))`. Region adds `r sprintf("%.2f", gl("dis", "Region"))`, almost all of it London. Without London region adds nothing (`r sprintf("%+.2f", gl("dis", "Region", "Without London"))`), and ethnic mix accounts for all of the fall (`r sprintf("%.2f", gl("dis", gterm, "Without London"))`, against a fall of `r sprintf("%.2f", gl("dis", "base", "Without London") - gl("dis", "full", "Without London"))`, since the other parts are slightly negative overall). Density, health, cars, deprivation and needs each do little once ethnic mix is held, and their parts roughly cancel.

@fig-ladder shows it directly, using DfE's count of [pupils by ethnicity and free school meals in each authority](https://explore-education-statistics.service.gov.uk/find-statistics/school-pupils-and-their-characteristics), so that each group of pupils is compared on its own ethnic mix.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ladder
#| fig-cap: "The slope of absence on distance, all years pooled, with 95% intervals, as controls are added. Ethnic mix is the shares of that group of pupils who are White British, Asian, Black and of mixed heritage, by authority and year. Points of absence per kilometre."
#| fig-height: 6.4
SETS <- c("Share and urbanity", "And White British share of this group", "And full ethnic mix of this group", "And region", "And ethnic mix and region", "And ethnic mix, region and density", "And every control")
lz <- R$group_mix |> filter(sample %in% c("All authorities", "Without London", "Mostly urban, without London", "Less urban")) |>
  mutate(group = factor(unname(GRL[group]), rev(names(GROUP_COL)[1:3])), set = factor(set, rev(SETS)), sample = factor(sample, c("All authorities", "Without London", "Mostly urban, without London", "Less urban")))
ggplot(lz, aes(b, set, colour = group)) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = GREY, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = b - 1.96 * se, xmax = b + 1.96 * se), position = position_dodge(width = 0.65), size = 0.25, linewidth = 0.55) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = GROUP_COL, breaks = names(GROUP_COL)[1:3], name = NULL) + facet_wrap(~sample, ncol = 2) +
  labs(x = "Points of absence per km", y = NULL) + theme_note()
```

Why would ethnic mix do this? In 2024/25 the White British share of an authority's disadvantaged pupils correlates with how far its deprived neighbourhoods are from a school (r = `r sprintf("%.2f", R$mix_cor$cor_wb_km)`), since diverse places tend to be dense places with schools close together. On its own that share accounts for `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * R$mix_cor$r2)` of the variation in disadvantaged absence between authorities. So where schools are close, disadvantaged pupils also tend to be from groups with higher attendance, and a simple plot such as @fig-absence credits distance with that. This says nothing about why attendance differs between groups: ethnic mix stands in for migration histories, family and community ties and much else, none of which the data can separate.

**Confounding or mediation?** A mediator lies on the path: distance would change it, and it would change absence. A confounder drives both. The evidence points to confounding.

- A longer journey to school does not change the ethnic mix of a place, so ethnic mix cannot sensibly be a mediator of distance. It is a confounder, or composition.
- The obvious candidates for mediation contribute little. Households with no car and population density barely move the slope once ethnic mix is held (@fig-gelbach). That does not rule out mediation, because authority-wide averages are a poor measure of how any one family travels.

The test of composition is whether the link holds within one ethnic group. DfE publishes absence by ethnic group for each authority, though not split by disadvantage.

```{r}
#| label: fig-eth-ci
#| fig-cap: !expr paste("Within each ethnic group, points of secondary absence per kilometre, the estimates in the table below.", CI_NOTE)
#| fig-height: 4.6
R$within_eth |> filter(phase == "sec", control == "Share, urban", sample %in% c("All authorities", "Without London", "Mostly urban, without London")) |>
  mutate(eth = factor(eth, c("White British", "Asian", "Black", "Mixed heritage"))) |> arrange(eth) |>
  transmute(row = as.character(eth), group = distance, b, se, panel = sample) |> ci_plot("Points of absence per km", ncol = 3)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-eth
#| tbl-cap: "Within each ethnic group: points of secondary absence per kilometre between an authority's deprived neighbourhoods and a school, and from where that group lives (the mean over all neighbourhoods weighted by the group's Census residents), all years pooled, allowing for the share disadvantaged and how urban the authority is, with 95% intervals. All pupils in each ethnic group; DfE does not split these by disadvantage. Authorities with at least 100 pupils in the group."
R$within_eth |> filter(phase == "sec", control == "Share, urban", sample %in% c("All authorities", "Without London", "Mostly urban, without London")) |>
  mutate(v = ci2(b, se)) |> select(`Ethnic group` = eth, Distance = distance, sample, v) |> pivot_wider(names_from = sample, values_from = v) |>
  mutate(`Ethnic group` = factor(`Ethnic group`, c("White British", "Asian", "Black", "Mixed heritage"))) |> arrange(`Ethnic group`, Distance) |> kt(align = "llrrr")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## The model behind this table

$$\text{absence}^{(e)}_{a,t} = \beta\,\text{distance}^{(e)}_{a} + \gamma_1\,\text{share}_{a,t} + \gamma_2\,\text{urban\_share}_{a} + \tau_t + \varepsilon_{a,t}$$

```r
# R/19_distance_absence.R: one ethnic group e at a time, authorities with 100+ pupils in it
feols(overall ~ near_dep + share + urban_share | tp, data = E, cluster = ~la)       # from deprived neighbourhoods
feols(overall ~ near_e + share + urban_share | tp, data = E, cluster = ~la)       # from where the group lives
```

`overall` is the absence of all pupils of ethnic group $e$ in the authority (DfE does not split these by disadvantage). `near_e` is the mean straight-line km to a school over all neighbourhoods, weighted by the group's Census residents.
:::

The slope mostly goes. For White British pupils it is `r sprintf("%+.2f", we("White British", "All authorities"))` per kilometre, and about zero outside London (`r sprintf("%+.2f", we("White British", "Without London"))`) and in mostly urban authorities outside London (`r sprintf("%+.2f", we("White British", "Mostly urban, without London"))`). For Asian and Black pupils it is below zero. Directly standardising says the same for all pupils: of a slope of `r sprintf("%.2f", dm("Actual absence"))`, `r sprintf("%.2f", dm("Explained by ethnic mix"))` is what each authority's ethnic mix would give at national rates, and `r sprintf("%.2f", dm("Beyond ethnic mix"))` is left (t = `r sprintf("%.1f", dm("Beyond ethnic mix") / dm("Beyond ethnic mix", "se"))`), or `r sprintf("%.2f", dm("Beyond ethnic mix", s = "Without London"))` without London (t = `r sprintf("%.1f", dm("Beyond ethnic mix", s = "Without London") / dm("Beyond ethnic mix", s = "Without London", "se"))`).

This test cannot settle things for disadvantaged pupils, because most pupils in each ethnic group are not disadvantaged, and non-disadvantaged pupils show little slope anyway. A clear link among disadvantaged White British pupils could be hidden inside a flat line for all White British pupils. DfE publishes nothing that would show it.

#### Is anything left once the controls are in? {#sec-left}

```{r}
#| label: fig-left-ci
#| fig-cap: !expr paste("What is left with every control, in points of absence per kilometre, the estimates in the table below.", CI_NOTE)
#| fig-height: 3.6
R$group_mix |> filter(set == "And every control") |> transmute(row = sample, group = unname(GRL[group]), b, se) |> ci_plot("Points of absence per km, given every control")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-left
#| tbl-cap: "What is left in the fullest model: share, urbanity, the group's ethnic mix, region, seven Census measures and six measures of pupils. Points of absence per kilometre, all years pooled, with 95% intervals. Explained is the share of the variation in distance that those controls account for."
R$group_mix |> filter(set == "And every control") |> mutate(v = ci2(b, se)) |> select(sample, group, v) |> pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = v) |>
  left_join(R$full_models |> filter(group == "dis") |> transmute(sample, `Explained` = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * r2_dist), Authorities = las), by = "sample") |>
  transmute(Sample = sample, Authorities, `All pupils` = all, Disadvantaged = dis, `Non-disadvantaged` = non, `Explained`) |> kt(align = "lrrrrr")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## The model behind this table

$$\text{absence}_{a,t} = \beta\,\text{near\_dep}_{a,t} + \underbrace{\gamma_1\,\text{share} + \gamma_2\,\text{urban\_share}}_{\text{share and urbanity}} + \underbrace{\boldsymbol{\delta}'\,\text{ethnic mix}}_{4} + \underbrace{\rho_{\text{region}}}_{9} + \underbrace{\boldsymbol{\kappa}'\,\text{Census}}_{7} + \underbrace{\boldsymbol{\pi}'\,\text{pupils}}_{6} + \tau_t + \varepsilon_{a,t}$$

```r
# R/19_distance_absence.R: authorities by year, secondary, for each group (dis, non, all) and sample
feols(overall ~ near_dep + share + urban_share +
        eth_wb + eth_asian + eth_black + eth_mixed +                                    # ethnic mix of this group
        gor_name +                                                                      # region
        graduates + bad_health + white_british + social_rent + no_car + deprived + log_density +   # Census
        sen_sup + ehcp + ks2_c + eal + wbri + mobile                                     # pupils
      | tp, data = A, cluster = ~la)
# "Explained": R-squared of the same controls predicting near_dep
feols(near_dep ~ share + urban_share + eth_wb + ... + mobile | tp, data = A)
```

$\beta$ is the table's figure. The ethnic mix is the shares of that group's pupils who are White British, Asian, Black and of mixed heritage; the Census measures are of the authority's residents and households; the pupil measures are of its secondary pupils. Every variable is in [the glossary](method.qmd#sec-model-variables).
:::

Across all authorities, no clear slope is left for any group: `r sprintf("%+.2f", gm("dis", "And every control"))` for disadvantaged pupils, with an interval from `r sprintf("%+.1f", gm("dis", "And every control") - 1.96 * gm("dis", "And every control", col = "se"))` to `r sprintf("%+.1f", gm("dis", "And every control") + 1.96 * gm("dis", "And every control", col = "se"))`. Adding distance to that model leaves its fit unchanged (R² `r sprintf("%.3f", fm("dis", "r2_without"))` to `r sprintf("%.3f", fm("dis", "r2_with"))`). But that interval does not mean zero. It still allows a little over one point per kilometre, and the controls account for `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * fm("dis", "r2_dist"))` of the variation in distance, so the model has little left to work with, and 28 terms for `r nrow(la)` authorities.

The link survives further in towns and cities. In mostly urban authorities it is `r sprintf("%+.2f", gm("dis", "And every control", "Mostly urban"))` with every control (t = `r sprintf("%.1f", gm("dis", "And every control", "Mostly urban") / gm("dis", "And every control", "Mostly urban", "se"))`). Outside London it is `r sprintf("%+.2f", gm("dis", "And ethnic mix and region", "Mostly urban, without London"))` given ethnic mix and region (t = `r sprintf("%.1f", gm("dis", "And ethnic mix and region", "Mostly urban, without London") / gm("dis", "And ethnic mix and region", "Mostly urban, without London", "se"))`), and `r sprintf("%+.2f", gm("dis", "And every control", "Mostly urban, without London"))` with every control, when its interval includes zero. In less urban authorities there is nothing at any stage.

Other designs are not subject to this limit, and they are in the sections that follow. Within authorities the link stays in the most deprived neighbourhoods given Census character, including their White British residents ([below](#sec-within)). At school level it survives the school's own ethnic make-up in every year ([below](#sec-school)).

#### A falsification test: primary schools {#sec-primary}

If the link is about getting to a secondary school, the distance to a secondary school should say little about absence in primary schools. If it is about the place, it should predict both. The same children and families are involved, so this is a sharp test.

```{r}
#| label: fig-primary
#| fig-cap: "The distance from deprived neighbourhoods to a secondary school against absence in secondary schools, in primary schools, and the step up between them in the same authority and year, all years pooled, with 95% intervals. Points of absence per kilometre, allowing for the share disadvantaged and how urban the authority is."
#| fig-height: 5.6
pz <- bind_rows(lapply(c(dis = "dis", non = "non", all = "all"), function(g) {
  bind_rows(
    tibble(sample = "All authorities", kind = "Secondary", b = pl(paste0(g, "_sec")), se = pl(paste0(g, "_sec"), col = "se")),
    tibble(sample = "All authorities", kind = "Primary", b = pl(paste0(g, "_pri")), se = pl(paste0(g, "_pri"), col = "se")),
    tibble(sample = "All authorities", kind = "Secondary minus primary", b = pl(paste0("step_", g)), se = pl(paste0("step_", g), col = "se")),
    tibble(sample = "Without London", kind = "Secondary", b = pl(paste0(g, "_sec"), s = "Without London"), se = pl(paste0(g, "_sec"), s = "Without London", col = "se")),
    tibble(sample = "Without London", kind = "Primary", b = pl(paste0(g, "_pri"), s = "Without London"), se = pl(paste0(g, "_pri"), s = "Without London", col = "se")),
    tibble(sample = "Without London", kind = "Secondary minus primary", b = pl(paste0("step_", g), s = "Without London"), se = pl(paste0("step_", g), s = "Without London", col = "se")),
    tibble(sample = "Mostly urban, without London", kind = "Secondary", b = oa(g, "None beyond share and urbanity", "Mostly urban, without London"), se = oa(g, "None beyond share and urbanity", "Mostly urban, without London", "se")),
    tibble(sample = "Mostly urban, without London", kind = "Primary", b = us(paste0(g, "_pri")), se = us(paste0(g, "_pri"), col = "se")),
    tibble(sample = "Mostly urban, without London", kind = "Secondary minus primary", b = us(paste0("step_", g)), se = us(paste0("step_", g), col = "se"))) |> mutate(group = g)
})) |> mutate(group = factor(unname(GRL[group]), rev(names(GROUP_COL)[1:3])), kind = factor(kind, c("Secondary minus primary", "Primary", "Secondary")),
              sample = factor(sample, c("All authorities", "Without London", "Mostly urban, without London")))
ggplot(pz, aes(b, group, colour = kind)) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = GREY, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = b - 1.96 * se, xmax = b + 1.96 * se), position = position_dodge(width = 0.6), size = 0.3, linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Secondary" = BPURPLE, "Primary" = BLUE, "Secondary minus primary" = DPURPLE), breaks = c("Secondary", "Primary", "Secondary minus primary"), name = NULL) +
  facet_wrap(~sample, ncol = 1) + labs(x = "Points of absence per km", y = NULL) + theme_note()
```

It passes on these controls. For disadvantaged pupils the slope is `r sprintf("%+.1f", pl("dis_sec"))` in secondary schools and `r sprintf("%+.1f", pl("dis_pri"))` in primary, and it is `r sprintf("%+.1f", pl("step_dis"))` on the step up from primary to secondary within the same authority and year, which sets aside anything about a place that affects both phases. For non-disadvantaged pupils the primary slope is `r sprintf("%+.1f", pl("non_pri"))`, below zero. The step up is steeper for disadvantaged pupils than for non-disadvantaged pupils by `r sprintf("%.1f", pl("step_gap"))` points per kilometre (t = `r sprintf("%.1f", pl("step_gap") / pl("step_gap", col = "se"))`), or `r sprintf("%.1f", pl("step_gap", s = "Without London"))` without London (t = `r sprintf("%.1f", pl("step_gap", s = "Without London") / pl("step_gap", s = "Without London", col = "se"))`).

The small primary slope for disadvantaged pupils is not zero, which suggests some of the secondary slope is the place. Distance to a primary school itself goes with primary absence for disadvantaged pupils (`r sprintf("%+.1f", R$pri_own$b_pri[R$pri_own$out == "dis_pri"])` per kilometre, t = `r sprintf("%.1f", R$pri_own$b_pri[R$pri_own$out == "dis_pri"] / R$pri_own$se_pri[R$pri_own$out == "dis_pri"])`), though primary schools are so close that a kilometre is a long way. The test is less clear once ethnic mix is held, because the difference in attendance between ethnic groups is itself wider in secondary school than in primary. Across all authorities the step up for disadvantaged pupils falls to `r sprintf("%+.2f", gp("dis", "Secondary minus primary", "All authorities"))` (t = `r sprintf("%.1f", gp("dis", "Secondary minus primary", "All authorities") / gp("dis", "Secondary minus primary", "All authorities", "se"))`). In mostly urban authorities outside London the test still passes: given ethnic mix and region, `r sprintf("%+.1f", gm("dis", "And ethnic mix and region", "Mostly urban, without London"))` in secondary, `r sprintf("%+.1f", gp("dis", "Primary, and region"))` in primary, and `r sprintf("%+.1f", gp("dis", "Secondary minus primary, and region"))` on the step up (t = `r sprintf("%.1f", gp("dis", "Secondary minus primary, and region") / gp("dis", "Secondary minus primary, and region", col = "se"))`).

#### Within the same authority {#sec-within}

Everything so far compares one authority with another, so anything about a whole place can be mistaken for distance. [A second DfE data set](https://explore-education-statistics.service.gov.uk/data-catalogue/data-set/6dd7f70e-440f-4c0f-b8d1-056678c25301) offers a stronger test. For 2023/24 and 2024/25 it gives absence by where pupils *live*, not where they go to school, in each authority, by the national tenth of the Income Deprivation Affecting Children Index (IDACI) of their home neighbourhood. Those tenths can be matched to the distance from the same neighbourhoods, giving `r format(R$n_cells, big.mark = ",")` groups of pupils in `r R$valid$las` authorities. The number of pupils in each group lines up closely with the Census count of children (r = `r sprintf("%.2f", R$valid$r)`). DfE does not split this file by disadvantage, so it describes all pupils living in each kind of neighbourhood.

Brighton and Hove stands out in it (@fig-bh-deciles). Across England, children in the most deprived neighbourhoods live nearest a school. In Brighton and Hove they live furthest away, and absence and persistent absence climb much more steeply with deprivation than in England.

```{r}
#| label: fig-bh-deciles
#| fig-cap: "Pupils in state-funded secondary schools, 2024/25, by the national IDACI tenth of the neighbourhood where they live (1 = most deprived): straight-line distance to a school, overall absence, and the share who are persistently absent. All pupils; DfE does not publish this by disadvantage. DfE, absence by pupil residence; IoD 2019; Census 2021; Get Information About Schools."
#| fig-height: 3.8
dz <- R$deciles |> filter(phase == "sec") |> select(place, dec, `Distance to nearest school (km)` = near, `Absence (% of sessions)` = overall, `Persistently absent (% of pupils)` = persistent) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(place, dec)) |> mutate(name = factor(name, c("Distance to nearest school (km)", "Absence (% of sessions)", "Persistently absent (% of pupils)")))
ggplot(dz, aes(dec, value, colour = place)) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) + geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Brighton and Hove" = BPURPLE, "England" = INK), name = NULL) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 4, 7, 10)) + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA)) +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") + labs(x = "IDACI tenth of home neighbourhood (1 = most deprived)", y = NULL) + theme_note()
```

The children in the city's most deprived tenth of neighbourhoods live `r sprintf("%.2f", dc(BH, 1, "near"))` km from a school, against `r sprintf("%.2f", dc("England", 1, "near"))` km for that tenth across England. They miss `r sprintf("%.1f%%", dc(BH, 1, "overall"))` of sessions against `r sprintf("%.1f%%", dc("England", 1, "overall"))`, and `r sprintf("%.0f%%", dc(BH, 1, "persistent"))` are persistently absent against `r sprintf("%.0f%%", dc("England", 1, "persistent"))`.

```{r}
#| label: fig-within-ci
#| fig-cap: !expr paste("Points of absence per kilometre for pupils in each kind of neighbourhood, between and within authorities, the estimates in the table below. All pupils.", CI_NOTE)
#| fig-height: 3.6
R$between |> mutate(band = sub(" three tenths| four tenths", "", band)) |> transmute(row = comparison, group = band, b, se) |> ci_plot("Points of absence per km")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-within
#| tbl-cap: "Points of absence per kilometre for secondary pupils living in each kind of neighbourhood, 2023/24 and 2024/25, weighted by pupils, with 95% intervals and errors clustered by authority. All pupils in those neighbourhoods. Between authorities compares the same IDACI tenth across authorities; within authorities compares neighbourhoods in the same authority, against the national pattern for each tenth. Census character is how urban and dense the neighbourhoods are, and their graduates, White British residents, households with no car, social renting and bad health."
R$between |> mutate(v = ci2(b, se), band = sub(" three tenths| four tenths", "", band)) |> select(Comparison = comparison, band, v) |> pivot_wider(names_from = band, values_from = v) |>
  select(Comparison, `Most deprived`, Middle, `Least deprived`) |> kt(align = "lrrr") |>
  kableExtra::add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Neighbourhoods by IDACI tenth" = 3))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## The model behind this table

$$\text{absence}_{a,d,t} = \beta\,\text{near}_{a,d} + \boldsymbol{\gamma}'\mathbf{c}_{a,d} + \alpha_{a,t} + \delta_{d,t} + \varepsilon_{a,d,t}$$

```r
# R/19_distance_absence.R: one row per authority a, IDACI tenth d and year t, secondary, weighted by pupils
feols(overall ~ near | dec^tp,                     data = B, weights = ~enrol, cluster = ~la)   # between authorities
feols(overall ~ near + urban_c + dens_c | dec^tp,  ...)                                         # between, given urban and dense
feols(overall ~ near | la^tp + dec^tp,             ...)                                         # within authorities
feols(overall ~ near + urban_c + dens_c + grad_c + wbri_c + nocar_c + social_c + bad_c | la^tp + dec^tp, ...)   # within, given Census character
```

`overall` is absence of all pupils living in that tenth of that authority (DfE, absence by pupil residence). `near` is the child-weighted mean straight-line km from those neighbourhoods to the nearest school. $\alpha_{a,t}$ (authority by year) compares neighbourhoods within one authority; $\delta_{d,t}$ (tenth by year) takes out the national pattern for each tenth. The `_c` terms are the Census character of the neighbourhoods, centred.
:::

Three things follow.

- **Most of the slope between authorities is not there within them.** For the most deprived three tenths it is `r sprintf("%+.1f", bw("Most deprived three tenths", "Between authorities"))` per kilometre between authorities, and `r sprintf("%+.2f", bw("Most deprived three tenths", "Within authorities"))` within them, or `r sprintf("%+.2f", bw("Most deprived three tenths", "Within, given Census character"))` given Census character. Part of that fall will be noise, because the distance for a tenth of an authority's neighbourhoods is a rough average of places that can be far apart. Even so, the safer reading is that most of the slope between authorities is about the authorities, which fits what ethnic mix does above. Holding Census character raises the slope, because within an authority the further neighbourhoods tend to be less urban and less dense (r = `r sprintf("%.2f", R$within_sort[["urban"]])` and `r sprintf("%.2f", R$within_sort[["density"]])`), and differ little in their White British share (r = `r sprintf("%.2f", R$within_sort[["wbri"]])`). So the clearer estimate depends on that adjustment: without it the interval includes zero.
- **What remains is where it should be.** Within authorities, given Census character, the link is clear only for pupils in the most deprived three tenths. It is steeper there than in the least deprived three tenths by `r sprintf("%.2f", R$band_diff$diff)` points per kilometre (t = `r sprintf("%.1f", R$band_diff$diff / R$band_diff$se)`). It is similar in each year (`r sprintf("%+.2f", R$band_year$b[R$band_year$tp == 202324])` and `r sprintf("%+.2f", R$band_year$b[R$band_year$tp == 202425])`), without London (`r sprintf("%+.2f", bp("Most deprived three tenths", "sec", "Without London"))`) and without Brighton and Hove (`r sprintf("%+.2f", bp("Most deprived three tenths", "sec", "Without Brighton and Hove"))`).
- **It is much weaker in primary schools.** In the same neighbourhoods the primary slope is `r sprintf("%+.2f", bp2("pri"))`, with an interval that includes zero, against `r sprintf("%+.2f", bp2("sec"))` in secondary.
