The persistent absence result is `r sprintf("%+.1f", bk("persistent", "sec"))` points of pupils per kilometre in secondary (t = `r sprintf("%.1f", bk("persistent", "sec") / bk("persistent", "sec", "se"))`) and `r sprintf("%+.1f", bk("persistent", "pri"))` in primary (t = `r sprintf("%.1f", bk("persistent", "pri") / bk("persistent", "pri", "se"))`).

```{r}
#| label: fig-deciles
#| fig-cap: "Points of absence per kilometre for pupils living in each national IDACI tenth of neighbourhood, comparing authorities within each tenth, given Census character, 2023/24 and 2024/25, with 95% intervals. All pupils in those neighbourhoods."
#| fig-height: 3.8
dd1 <- R$dec1 |> mutate(phase = factor(ifelse(phase == "sec", "Secondary", "Primary"), c("Secondary", "Primary")))
ggplot(dd1, aes(dec, b, colour = phase)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GREY, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = b - 1.96 * se, ymax = b + 1.96 * se), position = position_dodge(width = 0.45), size = 0.35, linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Secondary" = BPURPLE, "Primary" = BLUE), name = NULL) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +
  labs(x = "IDACI tenth of home neighbourhood (1 = most deprived)", y = "Points of absence per km") + theme_note()
```

#### When the school network changes {#sec-network}

The strongest test available would follow the same place as a school opens or closes nearby. @tbl-network does this for authorities and for schools. Very few authorities' distance moved much: only `r R$fe_var$n_changed` of `r R$fe_var$n` changed by 50 metres or more between 2018/19 and 2024/25. Brighton and Hove did not change at all. So these estimates are imprecise.

```{r}
#| label: fig-network-ci
#| fig-cap: !expr paste("When distance changes in the same place. Authorities, in points of absence per kilometre (left), and schools, per doubling of how far their nearest children live (right), the estimates in the table below.", CI_NOTE)
#| fig-height: 3.4
fs <- R$sch_fe |> filter(outcome == "overall")
(R$fe_la |> filter(out %in% c("dis_sec", "non_sec", "all_sec", "dis_pri", "non_pri", "all_pri")) |>
   transmute(row = ifelse(endsWith(out, "sec"), "Secondary", "Primary"), group = unname(GRL[sub("_.*", "", out)]), b, se) |> ci_plot("Authorities: points per km")) +
(tibble(row = c("Schools", "Schools, against others in the authority that year"), b = c(fs$b, fs$b_la), se = c(fs$se, fs$se_la)) |> ci_plot("Schools: points per doubling", wrap = 26))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-network
#| tbl-cap: "When distance changes in the same place. Authority rows use authority and year effects and allow for the share disadvantaged, in points of absence per kilometre. School rows use school and year effects and allow for intake, in points of overall absence for each doubling of how far a school's nearest children live, with the second row adding effects for each authority in each year. DfE publishes school absence for all pupils only. 95% intervals; errors clustered by authority or by school."
fe <- function(k) { x <- R$fe_la |> filter(out == k); ci2(x$b, x$se) }
fs <- R$sch_fe |> filter(outcome == "overall")
tibble(`Comparison` = c("Authorities: secondary, disadvantaged", "Authorities: secondary, non-disadvantaged", "Authorities: secondary, all pupils", "Authorities: primary, disadvantaged", "Authorities: primary, non-disadvantaged", "Authorities: primary, all pupils", "Schools: all pupils", "Schools: all pupils, against others in the authority that year"),
       Estimate = c(fe("dis_sec"), fe("non_sec"), fe("all_sec"), fe("dis_pri"), fe("non_pri"), fe("all_pri"), ci2(fs$b, fs$se), ci2(fs$b_la, fs$se_la))) |> kt(align = "lr")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## The model behind this table

$$\text{absence}_{a,t} = \beta\,\text{near\_dep}_{a,t} + \gamma\,\text{share}_{a,t} + \alpha_a + \tau_t + \varepsilon_{a,t} \qquad \text{absence}_{s,t} = \beta\,\log_2 \text{km}_{s,t} + \boldsymbol{\gamma}'\mathbf{z}_{s,t} + \alpha_s + \tau_t + \varepsilon_{s,t}$$

```r
# R/19_distance_absence.R
feols(dis_sec ~ near_dep + share | la + tp, data = wide, cluster = ~la)                     # authorities; likewise each group and phase
feols(overall ~ l2 + fsm_c + sen_sup + ehcp + eal + girls + lsize | cid + tp, data = S, cluster = ~cid)          # schools
feols(overall ~ l2 + l2:fsm_c + fsm_c + sen_sup + ehcp + eal + girls + lsize | cid + la_g^tp, data = S, cluster = ~cid)   # schools, against others in the authority that year
```

With an effect $\alpha$ for each authority or school, $\beta$ is estimated only from changes over time in the same place, as schools open, close and change. `l2` is $\log_2$ of the mean straight-line km of the school's nearest children; `cid` follows a school through changes of number.
:::

All point in the expected direction, and at the secondary level the authority estimate for disadvantaged pupils (`r sprintf("%+.1f", R$fe_la$b[R$fe_la$out == "dis_sec"])`) is similar in size to the slope between authorities. But its interval is wide and includes zero. At school level, `r R$sch_move$changed10` of `r format(R$sch_move$schools, big.mark = ",")` schools saw their nearest children's distance change by 10% or more. These are consistent with distance mattering, but do not establish it. New schools also open where populations are growing, so these changes are not random.

#### What kind of absence? {#sec-kinds-la}

```{r}
#| label: fig-kinds-la-ci
#| fig-cap: !expr paste("Points per kilometre by kind of absence, the estimates in the table below. Persistent absence is in points of pupils, so its scale differs.", CI_NOTE)
#| fig-height: 4.6
R$kinds_la |> mutate(Kind = c(overall = "Overall", illness = "Illness", unauth = "Unauthorised", persistent = "Persistent absence")[outcome]) |>
  transmute(row = sample, group = unname(GRL[group]), b, se, panel = Kind) |> ci_plot("Points per km", free_x = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-kinds-la
#| tbl-cap: "Points per kilometre by kind of absence, all years pooled, allowing for the share disadvantaged and how urban the authority is, with 95% intervals. Persistent absence is the share of pupils missing 10% or more of sessions; the others are shares of sessions."
KL <- c(overall = "Overall", illness = "Illness", unauth = "Unauthorised", persistent = "Persistent absence")
R$kinds_la |> mutate(v = ci2(b, se), Group = unname(GRL[group]), Kind = KL[outcome]) |> select(Group, Kind, Mean = mean, sample, v) |> pivot_wider(names_from = sample, values_from = v) |>
  mutate(Group = factor(Group, names(GROUP_COL)[1:3]), Kind = factor(Kind, KL), Mean = sprintf("%.1f", Mean)) |> arrange(Group, Kind) |> kt(align = "llrrr")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## The model behind this table

$$\text{absence}^{(k)}_{a,t} = \beta\,\text{near\_dep}_{a,t} + \gamma_1\,\text{share}_{a,t} + \gamma_2\,\text{urban\_share}_{a} + \tau_t + \varepsilon_{a,t}$$

```r
# R/19_distance_absence.R: for each kind of absence k and group
feols(overall    ~ near_dep + share + urban_share | tp, data = A, cluster = ~la)
feols(illness    ~ near_dep + share + urban_share | tp, ...)
feols(unauth     ~ near_dep + share + urban_share | tp, ...)
feols(persistent ~ near_dep + share + urban_share | tp, ...)
```

`illness` and `unauth` are % of sessions missed for that reason; `persistent` is the % of pupils missing 10% or more.
:::

For disadvantaged pupils the link is mainly with unauthorised absence (`r sprintf("%+.1f", kl("dis", "unauth"))` of the `r sprintf("%+.1f", kl("dis", "overall"))` points) and hardly with illness (`r sprintf("%+.1f", kl("dis", "illness"))`). It is also large for persistent absence (`r sprintf("%+.1f", kl("dis", "persistent"))` points of pupils per kilometre, against a mean of `r sprintf("%.0f", kl("dis", "persistent", "mean"))`). The within-authority test agrees: for pupils in the most deprived three tenths of neighbourhoods, `r sprintf("%+.2f", bk3("unauth"))` of the `r sprintf("%+.2f", bk3("overall"))` is unauthorised. In mostly urban authorities outside London, given ethnic mix and region, it is `r sprintf("%+.1f", gk("dis", "unauth"))` unauthorised and `r sprintf("%+.1f", gk("dis", "illness"))` illness, and `r sprintf("%+.1f", gk("dis", "persistent"))` points of pupils persistently absent. That is what missed journeys might look like, more than ill health, though the data cannot say why pupils were absent. It matters here because Brighton and Hove's [overall gap with England is mostly coded as illness](absence_causes.qmd#sec-bh-codes), while its disadvantaged pupils are high on both.

#### Does it matter more in towns and cities? {#sec-urban}

The [roadmap](roadmap.qmd) asked whether distance matters more in towns and cities, where a longer journey may pass more places to stop, and less in the countryside, where long journeys are normal and often by school transport. Between authorities the answer looks like yes, and strikingly so.

```{r}
#| label: fig-urban-ci
#| fig-cap: !expr paste("Mostly urban and less urban authorities, in points of absence per kilometre, the estimates in the table below.", CI_NOTE)
#| fig-height: 6
bind_rows(
  R$urban_checks |> filter(!grepl("^Given", check)) |> transmute(row = check, group = unname(GRL[group]), b, se),
  R$group_mix |> filter(sample == "Mostly urban, without London", set %in% c("And full ethnic mix of this group", "And ethnic mix and region", "And ethnic mix, region and density", "And every control")) |>
    transmute(row = paste0("Mostly urban, without London, ", sub("^And ", "given ", set)), group = unname(GRL[group]), b, se),
  R$urb_sample |> filter(sample == "Less urban") |> transmute(row = ifelse(control == "Share, urban", "Less urban authorities", "Less urban authorities, given region"), group = unname(GRL[group]), b, se)) |>
  ci_plot("Points of absence per km")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-urban
#| tbl-cap: "Mostly urban authorities outside London (at least 80% of 10 to 14 year olds in urban neighbourhoods), and less urban authorities, all years pooled. Points of absence per kilometre with 95% intervals. All rows allow for the share disadvantaged and how urban the authority is."
ucr <- R$urban_checks |> filter(!grepl("^Given", check)) |> mutate(v = ci2(b, se)) |> select(Sample = check, group, v) |> pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = v)
ugm <- R$group_mix |> filter(sample == "Mostly urban, without London", set %in% c("And full ethnic mix of this group", "And ethnic mix and region", "And ethnic mix, region and density", "And every control")) |> mutate(v = ci2(b, se), Sample = paste0("Mostly urban, without London, ", sub("^And ", "given ", set))) |> select(Sample, group, v) |> pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = v)
lur <- R$urb_sample |> filter(sample == "Less urban") |> mutate(v = ci2(b, se), Sample = ifelse(control == "Share, urban", "Less urban authorities", "Less urban authorities, given region")) |> select(Sample, group, v) |> pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = v)
bind_rows(ucr, ugm, lur) |> transmute(Sample, `All pupils` = all, Disadvantaged = dis, `Non-disadvantaged` = non) |> kt(align = "lrrr")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## The model behind this table

$$\text{absence}_{a,t} = \beta\,\text{near\_dep}_{a,t} + \gamma_1\,\text{share}_{a,t} + \gamma_2\,\text{urban\_share}_{a} + \boldsymbol{\delta}'\mathbf{x}_{a,t} + \tau_t + \varepsilon_{a,t}$$

```r
# R/19_distance_absence.R: mostly urban authorities (urban_share >= 80) outside London
feols(overall ~ near_dep + share + urban_share | tp, data = filter(A, urban_share >= 80, !london), cluster = ~la)
# ... without Brighton and Hove; without the five with most influence (Cook's distance, 2024/25)
# ... given the group's ethnic mix, region, density, or every control, as in the table of what is left
```
:::

In mostly urban authorities outside London, disadvantaged absence rises `r sprintf("%.1f", oa("dis", "None beyond share and urbanity", "Mostly urban, without London"))` points per kilometre, in every year, and `r sprintf("%.1f", gm("dis", "And ethnic mix and region", "Mostly urban, without London"))` given ethnic mix and region. It holds without Brighton and Hove (`r sprintf("%.1f", uc("dis", "And without Brighton and Hove"))`) and without the five most influential authorities (`r sprintf("%.1f", uc("dis", "And without the five most influential"))`). In less urban authorities the slope is `r sprintf("%+.1f", us2("dis"))`, with an interval around zero, in every year. Secondary minus primary tells the same story (`r sprintf("%+.1f", us("step_dis"))` against `r sprintf("%+.1f", us("step_dis", s = "Less urban"))`).

Two other tests do not agree, so this is suggestive rather than settled.

- **Within authorities** the slope for the most deprived neighbourhoods is about the same in less urban authorities (`r sprintf("%+.2f", bp("Most deprived three tenths", "sec", "Less urban authorities"))`) and in mostly urban ones (`r sprintf("%+.2f", bp("Most deprived three tenths", "sec", "Mostly urban authorities"))`).
- **By school** the slope is similar across kinds of place (@tbl-place), though the rural interval is wide.

One reading is that an average distance for a whole rural county says little about any one child's journey, so the authority test may simply not see rural effects. Journey times, and data on who gets school transport, are needed to settle it.

### By school, for all pupils {#sec-school}

DfE does not publish absence by disadvantage school by school, so this test is for all pupils, and the closest it can come is to ask whether the link is stronger in schools with more pupils on free school meals. For each school, its "nearest children" are those in the Output Areas for which it is the nearest school, and the measure is how far they live from it, typically `r kms(D$school_km$p50)` km (a tenth of schools under `r kms(D$school_km$p10)` km and a tenth over `r kms(D$school_km$p90)` km). It is a stand-in: pupils often go elsewhere. Selective schools, and schools that are nearest for fewer than 100 children, are left out. Models compare schools within the same local authority.

```{r}
#| label: fig-kinds-ci
#| fig-cap: !expr paste("Schools. Absence for each doubling of how far a school's nearest children live, and the extra for each 10 points of free school meals, the estimates in the table below.", CI_NOTE)
#| fig-height: 3.2
bind_rows(D$kinds |> transmute(row = outcome, b, se, panel = "Each doubling of distance"),
          D$kinds |> transmute(row = outcome, b = 10 * b_int, se = 10 * se_int, panel = "Extra, per 10 points of free school meals")) |>
  ci_plot("Points of absence", free_x = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-kinds
#| tbl-cap: "How a school's absence, autumn and spring 2025/26, goes with how far its nearest children live: the change for each doubling of the distance, with 95% intervals, given its pupils' disadvantage, English as an additional language, prior attainment, special needs, mobility, sex, neighbourhood education, age range and kind of place, within local authority. The last column is how much more each doubling goes with for each extra 10 points of free school meals at the school."
D$kinds |> transmute(`Kind of absence` = outcome, `Mean` = sprintf("%.1f", mean),
    `Each doubling of distance` = sprintf("%+.2f (%+.2f to %+.2f)", b, b - 1.96 * se, b + 1.96 * se),
    `Extra, per 10 points of FSM` = sprintf("%+.2f (%+.2f to %+.2f)", 10 * b_int, 10 * (b_int - 1.96 * se_int), 10 * (b_int + 1.96 * se_int))) |>
  kt(align = "lrrr")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## The model behind this table

$$\text{absence}_s = \beta\,\log_2 \text{km}_s + \theta\,(\log_2 \text{km}_s \times \text{fsm\_c}_s) + \boldsymbol{\gamma}'\mathbf{z}_s + \alpha_a + \varepsilon_s$$

```r
# R/18_distance.R: one row per school, autumn and spring 2025/26
feols(overall ~ l2 + fsm + eal + ks2_c + z_l4 + sen_sup + ehcp + mobile + girls + place + age16 | la, data = fr, cluster = ~la)
feols(overall ~ l2 * fsm_c + eal + ks2_c + z_l4 + sen_sup + ehcp + mobile + girls + place + age16 | la, ...)   # last column
```

$\beta$ is points of absence for each doubling of `km` (`l2` = $\log_2$ km), the mean straight-line distance of the school's nearest children; $\theta$ is the last column, the extra for each 10 points of free school meals (scaled). $\alpha_a$ compares schools in the same authority. The intake terms are those of Value Added v2.1: free school meals, English as an additional language, prior attainment, neighbourhood education (`z_l4`), special needs, mobility, girls, kind of place, and whether the school stops at 16.
:::

Each doubling goes with `r sprintf("%.2f", kn("Overall absence"))` points more absence, against a mean of `r sprintf("%.1f", kn("Overall absence", "mean"))`, which is small, as FFT found. It shows up in illness (`r sprintf("%+.2f", kn("Illness"))`) and in persistent absence (`r sprintf("%+.2f", kn("Persistent absence (% of pupils)"))` points of pupils), more clearly than in unauthorised absence (`r sprintf("%+.2f", kn("Unauthorised"))`). It is also stronger in schools with more disadvantaged pupils, which fits FFT's result and the authority test above.

@fig-school-years repeats this for each year, with each year's school network.

```{r}
#| label: fig-school-years
#| fig-cap: "All pupils, by school, each year: overall absence, autumn and spring, for each doubling of how far a school's nearest children live, and how much more that is for each extra 10 points of free school meals at the school, with 95% intervals, given intake, kind of place and authority. DfE publishes no split by disadvantage at school level. DfE published no 2019/20, and 2020/21 is left out, as on How school absence changes."
#| fig-height: 3.6
sz <- bind_rows(sy_all |> transmute(tp, panel = "Each doubling of distance", b, se),
                sy_all |> transmute(tp, panel = "Extra, per 10 points of free school meals", b = 10 * b_int, se = 10 * se_int)) |>
  mutate(year = factor(ylab(tp), ylab(sort(unique(tp)))))
ggplot(sz, aes(year, b)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GREY, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = b - 1.96 * se, ymax = b + 1.96 * se), colour = GROUP_COL[["All pupils"]], size = 0.35, linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~panel) + labs(x = NULL, y = "Points of absence") + theme_note() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1))
```

The link appears in all `r nrow(sy_all)` years (from `r sprintf("%+.2f", min(sy_all$b))` to `r sprintf("%+.2f", max(sy_all$b))` for each doubling) and the extra for schools with more free school meals is above zero in every year, though not always clearly. The link is about twice as large since the pandemic as in 2018/19, when absence itself was much lower.

The models above leave out ethnic make-up. Since it matters so much between authorities, @tbl-school-wb adds each school's White British share. It takes about a quarter off the slope for overall absence, and the slope stays clear. The extra for schools with more free school meals does not change.

```{r}
#| label: fig-school-wb-ci
#| fig-cap: !expr paste("Schools, six years pooled. Each doubling of distance without and with the school's White British share, and the extra per 10 points of free school meals, the estimates in the table below.", CI_NOTE)
#| fig-height: 3.2
SWL <- c(overall = "Overall absence", illness = "Illness", unauth = "Unauthorised", persistent = "Persistent absence (% of pupils)")
bind_rows(R$sch_wb_pool |> transmute(row = SWL[outcome], b = b0, se = se0, group = "Without ethnic make-up", panel = "Each doubling of distance"),
          R$sch_wb_pool |> transmute(row = SWL[outcome], b = b1, se = se1, group = "With ethnic make-up", panel = "Each doubling of distance"),
          R$sch_wb_pool |> transmute(row = SWL[outcome], b = 10 * int1, se = 10 * se_int1, group = "With ethnic make-up", panel = "Extra, per 10 points of free school meals")) |>
  ci_plot("Points of absence", free_x = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-school-wb
#| tbl-cap: "All pupils, by school, six years pooled. Each doubling of how far a school's nearest children live, against other schools in the same authority and year, with and without the school's White British share (January 2026, held across years), and the extra for each 10 points of free school meals, with that share in the model. 95% intervals; errors clustered by authority."
SW <- c(overall = "Overall absence", illness = "Illness", unauth = "Unauthorised", persistent = "Persistent absence (% of pupils)")
R$sch_wb_pool |> transmute(`Kind of absence` = SW[outcome], `Without ethnic make-up` = ci2(b0, se0), `With ethnic make-up` = ci2(b1, se1), `Extra, per 10 points of FSM` = ci2(10 * int1, 10 * se_int1)) |> kt(align = "lrrr")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## The model behind this table

$$\text{absence}_{s,t} = \beta\,\log_2 \text{km}_s + \theta\,(\log_2 \text{km}_s \times \text{fsm\_c}_{s,t}) + \lambda\,\text{wbri}_s + \boldsymbol{\gamma}'\mathbf{z}_{s,t} + \alpha_{a,t} + \pi_{\text{place}} + \varepsilon_{s,t}$$

```r
# R/19_distance_absence.R: schools by year, 2018/19 to 2025/26
feols(overall ~ l2 + l2:fsm_c + fsm_c + sen_sup + ehcp + eal + girls + lsize | la_g^tp + place, data = S2, cluster = ~la_g)          # without
feols(overall ~ l2 + l2:fsm_c + wbri + fsm_c + sen_sup + ehcp + eal + girls + lsize | la_g^tp + place, data = S2, cluster = ~la_g)   # with the White British share
```

`wbri` is the school's White British share in January 2026, held across years. `lsize` is log of the school roll.
:::

**By kind of place.** @tbl-place splits schools by the same three kinds of place. The authority test is in [the section above](#sec-urban).

```{r}
#| label: fig-place-ci
#| fig-cap: !expr paste("Schools by kind of place. Absence for each doubling of distance, the estimates in the table below.", CI_NOTE)
#| fig-height: 2.8
bind_rows(lapply(c(UR, UF, RU), function(p) tibble(row = p, panel = c("Overall absence, 2025/26", "Above intake, 2021/22 to 2024/25"),
  b = c(kp("Overall absence", p), ex(p)), se = c(kp("Overall absence", p, "se"), ex(p, "se"))))) |> ci_plot("Points of absence per doubling", free_x = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-place
#| tbl-cap: "Absence for each doubling of how far a school's nearest children live, by kind of place, with 95% intervals: overall absence in autumn and spring 2025/26 as in the table above, and absence above what intake predicts, 2021/22 to 2024/25."
ord_p <- c(UR, UF, RU)
tibble(`Kind of place` = ord_p,
       Schools = vapply(ord_p, function(p) format(kp("Overall absence", p, "n"), big.mark = ","), ""),
       `Overall absence, 2025/26` = vapply(ord_p, function(p) { b <- kp("Overall absence", p); s <- kp("Overall absence", p, "se"); sprintf("%+.2f (%+.2f to %+.2f)", b, b - 1.96 * s, b + 1.96 * s) }, ""),
       `Above intake, 2021/22 to 2024/25` = vapply(ord_p, function(p) { b <- ex(p); s <- ex(p, "se"); sprintf("%+.2f (%+.2f to %+.2f)", b, b - 1.96 * s, b + 1.96 * s) }, "")) |>
  kt(align = "lrrr")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## The model behind this table

$$\text{absence}_s = \beta\,\log_2 \text{km}_s + \boldsymbol{\gamma}'\mathbf{z}_s + \alpha_a + \varepsilon_s \quad \text{(each kind of place separately)}$$

```r
# R/18_distance.R
feols(overall ~ l2 + fsm + eal + ks2_c + z_l4 + sen_sup + ehcp + mobile + girls + age16 | la, data = filter(fr, place == p), cluster = ~la)
feols(abs_excess ~ l2 | la, data = sch_abs, cluster = ~la)    # absence above what intake predicts, 2021/22 to 2024/25
```

`abs_excess` is a school's absence minus what its intake predicts, as on the area pages.
:::

The estimates are similar in size across kinds of place, but only urban schools near a major town or city, where most schools are, give a clear answer. There are fewer schools elsewhere and the intervals are wide, so this cannot show whether distance matters less in rural areas.

### And results? {#sec-results}

```{r}
#| label: fig-results-ci
#| fig-cap: !expr paste("Attainment 8 for each doubling of distance, % change, the estimates in the table below.", CI_NOTE)
#| fig-height: 2.6
D$results |> transmute(row = ifelse(absence_in_model, "With absence in the model", "Without absence in the model"), group, b, se) |> ci_plot("% change in Attainment 8 per doubling of distance")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-results
#| tbl-cap: "Attainment 8 for each doubling of how far a school's nearest children live, on the Value Added v2.1 specification for each group of pupils, with a school term, fitted on 2021/22 to 2024/25, with and without absence in the model. Percentage of Attainment 8, with 95% intervals."
D$results |> mutate(v = sprintf("%+.1f%% (%+.1f to %+.1f)", b, b - 1.96 * se, b + 1.96 * se),
                    m = ifelse(absence_in_model, "With absence in the model", "Without absence in the model")) |>
  select(Group = group, m, v) |> pivot_wider(names_from = m, values_from = v) |>
  select(Group, `Without absence in the model`, `With absence in the model`) |> kt(align = "lrr")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## The model behind this table

$$\log \text{Att8}_{s,t} = \beta\,\log_2 \text{km}_s + \boldsymbol{\gamma}'\mathbf{x}_{s,t} + u_t + u_{r} + u_{a(r)} + u_s + \varepsilon_{s,t}$$

```r
# R/18_distance.R: the Value Added v2.1 model for each group, with distance added
lmer(log(ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A) ~ l2 + log(PTFSM6CLA1A) + log(PERCTOT) + log(PNUMEAL) + ks2_c + ADMPOL_PT +
       z_l4 + sen_support + sen_ehcp + mobile + girls_school + age16 +
       (1 | year_label) + (1 | gor_name/LANAME) + (1 | URN), data = dg, REML = FALSE)
# "without absence in the model" drops log(PERCTOT)
```

$u$ are random effects for year, region, authority within region and school. $100\,(e^{\beta} - 1)$ is the % change in Attainment 8 for each doubling of distance, the table's figure. The terms are [those of v2.1](method.qmd#sec-full-spec).
:::

Schools whose nearest children live further away have lower results than their intake predicts, by more for disadvantaged pupils (`r sprintf("%.1f%%", rs("Disadvantaged", FALSE))` for each doubling) than for non-disadvantaged pupils (`r sprintf("%.1f%%", rs("Non-disadvantaged", FALSE))`) or all pupils (`r sprintf("%.1f%%", rs("All pupils", FALSE))`). Allowing for absence takes away about half of that for disadvantaged pupils. These are small differences, and part of what they measure may be the kind of place rather than the journey.

### What it adds up to {#sec-reading}

Taking the tests together:

- **Firm: the pattern.** Disadvantaged absence goes with distance in every year from 2018/19 and on every measure of distance, and it is much weaker in primary schools.
- **Firm: most of the slope in @fig-absence is not distance.** Ethnic mix accounts for nearly all of the fall across authorities, and is a confounder rather than a step on the path from distance to absence.
- **Likely: a smaller link of its own.** It appears in mostly urban authorities given ethnic mix and region, within authorities for pupils in the most deprived neighbourhoods, and between schools given their intake and ethnic make-up. It shows up in unauthorised and persistent absence. Three different designs, with different weaknesses, point the same way.
- **Not established: that distance causes it.** Network changes point the right way, but the estimates are imprecise and those changes are not random.

Brighton and Hove's disadvantaged pupils are close to the median authority for ethnic mix (`r sprintf("%.0f%%", R$bh_resid$wb)` White British, against `r sprintf("%.0f%%", R$bh_resid$wb_med)`), so ethnic mix does not explain its high absence. Given mix, region, share and urbanity, the city is `r sprintf("%.1f", R$bh_resid$resid_no_km)` points above expectation, `r ord(R$bh_resid$rank_no_km)` of `r R$bh_resid$n` authorities, and given distance too it is `r sprintf("%.1f", R$bh_resid$resid_km)` above, still `r ord(R$bh_resid$rank_km)`. So on this model distance explains only about `r sprintf("%.1f", R$bh_resid$resid_no_km - R$bh_resid$resid_km)` points of why the city stands out.

Its deprived neighbourhoods are `r kms(bh_u)` km further from a school than those of the median mostly urban authority outside London. On the urban estimates, from `r sprintf("%.1f", pool_r)` with every control to `r sprintf("%.1f", pool_s)` given ethnic mix, region and density, that would go with about `r sprintf("%.1f", bh_u * pool_r)` to `r sprintf("%.1f", bh_u * pool_s)` points of disadvantaged absence, out of the `r sprintf("%.1f", bh_gap_eng)` by which the city is above England. On the within-authority estimate, for all pupils in deprived neighbourhoods, it would be about `r sprintf("%.1f", (bh_near - med_la) * bh_w)`. So distance is a credible part of the city's problem, and not the main explanation for it. Journey times on the real networks may show more, because Brighton's hills and bus routes are what straight lines miss most.

## Journey times on the real networks {#sec-journeys}

Straight lines miss hills, the sea, street layouts and bus services. So for Brighton and Hove and the eight comparator places, every Output Area was routed to every state secondary school within 15 km with [r5r](https://ipeagit.github.io/r5r/), on OpenStreetMap streets and the Department for Transport's bus timetables for a school-term Tuesday, `r format(J$meta$date[1], "%e %B %Y")`. The method follows [the city's school system model](https://adamdennett.github.io/bh-school-system/), with a window of departures in place of a single time, and every source and setting is in [the methodology](method.qmd#sec-journey-method). This covers the journey to the *quickest* school from each neighbourhood, whichever school a child actually attends, and it is for all children: DfE publishes nothing on journeys by disadvantage.

```{r}
#| label: fig-journeys
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Minutes to the quickest state secondary school, for children in the most deprived third of each place's neighbourhoods and the rest, walking and by bus, and walking alone, on ", format(J$meta$date[1], "%e %B %Y"), ". Weighted by 10 to 14 year olds. Without allowing for hills.")
#| fig-height: 4.6
jl <- J$places |> filter(scenario %in% c("walk_bus", "walk")) |> mutate(scenario = factor(unname(J$scenarios[scenario]), unname(J$scenarios[c("walk_bus", "walk")])))
jord <- jl |> filter(scenario == J$scenarios[["walk_bus"]]) |> arrange(gap) |> pull(place)
jl <- jl |> mutate(place = factor(place, jord))
jp2 <- jl |> select(place, scenario, `Most deprived third` = t_dep, `Other neighbourhoods` = t_rest) |> pivot_longer(c(`Most deprived third`, `Other neighbourhoods`))
ggplot(jl, aes(y = place)) + geom_segment(aes(x = t_dep, xend = t_rest, yend = place), colour = LIGHT, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = jp2, aes(x = value, colour = name), size = 2.8) + scale_colour_manual(values = THIRD_COL, name = NULL) + scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, NA)) +
  facet_wrap(~scenario) + labs(x = "Minutes to the quickest school", y = NULL) + theme_note() + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(face = ifelse(jord == BH, "bold", "plain")))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-journeys
#| tbl-cap: "Minutes to the quickest state secondary school from the most deprived third of neighbourhoods and the rest, the difference, and the share of children over 30 minutes from a school by walking and bus. Dep. is the most deprived third; Rest is the other neighbourhoods. In order of the difference by walking and bus. Without allowing for hills."
jw <- J$places |> filter(scenario %in% c("walk_bus", "walk")) |> select(place, scenario, t_dep, t_rest, gap, over30_dep, over30_rest) |> pivot_wider(names_from = scenario, values_from = c(t_dep, t_rest, gap, over30_dep, over30_rest)) |> arrange(desc(gap_walk_bus))
jw |> transmute(Place = place, `Dep.` = sprintf("%.1f", t_dep_walk_bus), Rest = sprintf("%.1f", t_rest_walk_bus), Gap = sprintf("%+.1f", gap_walk_bus),
                `Dep. ` = sprintf("%.1f", t_dep_walk), `Rest ` = sprintf("%.1f", t_rest_walk), `Gap ` = sprintf("%+.1f", gap_walk),
                `Dep.  ` = sprintf("%.0f%%", over30_dep_walk_bus), `Rest  ` = sprintf("%.0f%%", over30_rest_walk_bus)) |> kt(align = "lrrrrrrrr") |>
  kableExtra::add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Walking and bus (min)" = 3, "Walking alone (min)" = 3, "Over 30 min" = 2))
```

**Brighton and Hove stands out on real journeys, as it does in straight lines.** Children in its most deprived third of neighbourhoods are `r sprintf("%.1f", jt(BH, "t_dep"))` minutes from a school by walking and bus, and the rest `r sprintf("%.1f", jt(BH, "t_rest"))`: `r sprintf("%.1f", jt(BH, "gap"))` minutes further. No other place is more than `r sprintf("%.1f", max(jbus$gap[jbus$place != BH]))` minutes further, and in `r sum(jbus$gap[jbus$place != BH] < 0)` of the eight the deprived neighbourhoods are nearer. Walking alone, the difference is `r sprintf("%.1f", jt(BH, "gap", "walk"))` minutes, more than twice the next largest (`r sprintf("%.1f", max(jwalk$gap[jwalk$place != BH]))`). `r sprintf("%.0f%%", jt(BH, "over45_dep"))` of children in the city's deprived neighbourhoods are more than 45 minutes from a school by walking and bus, against `r sprintf("%.0f%%", jt(BH, "over45_rest"))` of the rest.

**Buses narrow the gap but do not close it.** The difference falls by about half when buses are available in Brighton and Hove, from `r sprintf("%.1f", jt(BH, "gap", "walk"))` to `r sprintf("%.1f", jt(BH, "gap"))` minutes. In straight lines, measured here from Output Areas, the deprived neighbourhoods are `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * (jt(BH, "km_ratio") - 1))` further. In time it is `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * (jt(BH, "ratio", "walk") - 1))` further on foot and `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * (jt(BH, "ratio") - 1))` with buses. That assumes every family can use the bus, and the fare is not counted.

**Hastings looks different on this measure.** Journeys there are the longest of the nine for everyone (`r sprintf("%.0f", jt("Hastings", "t_all"))` minutes), but buses almost remove the difference between neighbourhoods (`r sprintf("%+.1f", jt("Hastings", "gap"))` minutes, against `r sprintf("%+.1f", jt("Hastings", "gap", "walk"))` on foot). In Hastings, `r sprintf("%.0f%%", jt("Hastings", "over30_dep"))` of children in deprived neighbourhoods and `r sprintf("%.0f%%", jt("Hastings", "over30_rest"))` of the rest are over 30 minutes from a school, so getting to school is hard across the town, whichever neighbourhood a child lives in.

```{r}
#| label: fig-journey-tenths
#| fig-cap: "Minutes to the quickest state secondary school for children in each national IDACI tenth of neighbourhood (1 = most deprived), in Brighton and Hove and the comparator places, where the place has at least 100 children in that tenth. Without allowing for hills."
#| fig-height: 4.2
tz <- J$tenths |> filter(children >= 100) |> mutate(scenario = factor(unname(J$scenarios[scenario]), unname(J$scenarios[c("walk_bus", "walk")])), who = ifelse(place == BH, BH, "Comparator places"))
ggplot(tz, aes(dec, t, group = place, colour = who, linewidth = who)) + geom_line() + geom_point(data = filter(tz, place == BH), size = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(c(BPURPLE, LIGHT), c(BH, "Comparator places")), name = NULL) + scale_linewidth_manual(values = setNames(c(1.1, 0.6), c(BH, "Comparator places")), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 4, 7, 10)) + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA)) + facet_wrap(~scenario) +
  labs(x = "IDACI tenth of home neighbourhood (1 = most deprived)", y = "Minutes to the quickest school") + theme_note()
```

The children in the city's most deprived tenth of neighbourhoods are `r sprintf("%.0f", jd(BH, 1))` minutes from a school by walking and bus, against `r sprintf("%.0f", jd(BH, 10))` minutes in its least deprived tenth.

### What the journeys are made of {#sec-interchanges}

A long journey is one thing and a journey with a change of bus is another. Getting off one bus to wait for the next is a point where a child can stay off, and one more connection to miss. So the routes were examined for the number of buses, leaving at 07:45, 08:00 and 08:15. These are still journeys to the quickest school, not to the school a child attends, so they understate the changes many children make.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-structure
#| tbl-cap: "How children would reach their quickest school, leaving at 07:45, 08:00 or 08:15, by the most deprived third of neighbourhoods (Dep.) and the rest (Rest). The share walking, the share needing two or more buses, and the average number of buses on each journey. Late if missed is how many minutes after 08:45 a child would arrive if they missed the last journey that gets there in time."
st3 <- as.data.table(J$str_third)[!is.na(third)][, t3 := ifelse(third, "dep", "rest")]
sw <- dcast(st3, place ~ t3, value.var = c("walk_only", "two_plus", "boardings", "late"))
sw[order(-two_plus_dep)][, .(Place = place, `Dep.` = sprintf("%.0f%%", walk_only_dep), Rest = sprintf("%.0f%%", walk_only_rest), `Dep. ` = sprintf("%.0f%%", two_plus_dep), `Rest ` = sprintf("%.0f%%", two_plus_rest), `Dep.  ` = sprintf("%.2f", boardings_dep), `Rest  ` = sprintf("%.2f", boardings_rest), `Dep.   ` = sprintf("%.1f", late_dep), `Rest   ` = sprintf("%.1f", late_rest))] |> kt(align = "lrrrrrrrr") |>
  kableExtra::add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Walking" = 2, "2+ buses" = 2, "Buses each" = 2, "Late (min)" = 2))
```

**Brighton and Hove's deprived neighbourhoods need the most changes.** `r sprintf("%.0f%%", js(BH, TRUE, "two_plus"))` of children in its most deprived third of neighbourhoods would need two or more buses to reach even the quickest school, against `r sprintf("%.0f%%", js(BH, FALSE, "two_plus"))` of the rest. In the other places shown, the highest figure for deprived neighbourhoods is `r sprintf("%.0f%%", max(st3$two_plus[st3$third & st3$place != BH]))`. `r sprintf("%.0f%%", js(BH, TRUE, "walk_only"))` of those children can walk fastest, against `r sprintf("%.0f%%", js(BH, FALSE, "walk_only"))` of the rest.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-interchanges
#| tbl-cap: "Where children in Brighton and Hove would change buses on the way to their quickest school: the busiest stops, by the 10 to 14 year olds whose journey changes there, averaged over the three departures. The nearest stop name is shown. Stops facing in different directions are listed separately."
as.data.table(J$interchanges)[place == BH][order(-children)][1:8, .(Stop = stop, `Children changing here` = round(children), `From the most deprived third` = round(dep_children))] |> kt(align = "lrr")
```

**This does not show up in absence, so far.** Within authorities and given each school's intake, schools whose nearest children need more buses do not have clearly higher absence (@tbl-journey-signal). That is `r J$n_school_model` schools in `r J$school_models$schools_la[1]` authorities, and uses journeys to the quickest school as a stand-in for real ones, so it is a weak test. Before distance is allowed for, the share needing two or more buses is clearer (t = `r sprintf("%.1f", jsm("Share needing two or more buses"))`), but that largely goes with distance. None of this rules out an effect on the children who do change buses.

```{r}
#| label: fig-journey-signal-ci
#| fig-cap: !expr paste("Schools in the nine routed places. Absence for one standard deviation more of each feature of the journey, given distance, the estimates in the table below.", CI_NOTE)
#| fig-height: 4
SLn <- c(`Share of children needing a bus` = 1, `Share needing two or more buses` = 2, `Buses per journey` = 3, `Minutes late if the last bus is missed` = 4, `Minutes on the journey` = 5, `Metres climbed to school` = 6, `Metres climbed home` = 7)
as.data.table(J$school_models)[term %in% names(SLn) & outcome %in% c("overall", "unauth", "persistent")][order(SLn[term])][,
  .(row = term, b = b_km * sd_x, se = se_km * sd_x, panel = c(overall = "Overall", unauth = "Unauthorised", persistent = "Persistent (% of pupils)")[outcome])] |>
  ci_plot("Points per standard deviation", ncol = 3, free_x = TRUE, wrap = 30)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-journey-signal
#| tbl-cap: "Schools in the routed places: absence for one standard deviation more of each feature of the journeys of the school's nearest children, within authority, given straight-line distance, free school meals, White British share, special needs and prior attainment, with t values. All pupils; DfE publishes no split by school. A guide only, with so few schools and authorities."
SL <- c(`Share of children needing a bus` = 1, `Share needing two or more buses` = 2, `Buses per journey` = 3, `Minutes late if the last bus is missed` = 4, `Minutes on the journey` = 5, `Metres climbed to school` = 6, `Metres climbed home` = 7)
as.data.table(J$school_models)[term %in% names(SL) & outcome %in% c("overall", "unauth", "persistent")][, v := sprintf("%+.2f (t = %.1f)", b_km * sd_x, b_km / se_km)] |> dcast(term ~ outcome, value.var = "v") |> (\(x) x[order(SL[term])])() |> (\(x) x[, .(`Feature of the journey` = term, `Overall absence` = overall, Unauthorised = unauth, `Persistent absence (% of pupils)` = persistent)])() |> kt(align = "lrrr")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## The model behind this table

$$\text{absence}_s = \beta\,x_s + \lambda\,\log_2 \text{km}_s + \boldsymbol{\gamma}'\mathbf{z}_s + \alpha_a + \varepsilon_s$$

```r
# R/21_journey_analysis.R: schools in the nine routed places
feols(overall ~ x + l2 + fsm + wbri + sen_sup + ks2_c | la, data = sch, cluster = ~la)
```

$x$ is the journey feature in the row, as the child-weighted mean over the school's nearest children; the table gives $\beta$ times the standard deviation of $x$.
:::

### School buses and missing them {#sec-school-buses}

Many places run dedicated school buses, with a few trips in the morning and a few back in the afternoon. In Brighton and Hove, for example, the 72 and 72A run from Whitehawk to Longhill's grounds, three trips each morning and three back. Miss one and the alternatives may be poor. These routes can be picked out of the timetables by their pattern, for [all of England](method.qmd#sec-journey-method): at most `r SB$rules$max_trips` trips a day, all within school travel hours, ending or starting by a state secondary school and no nearer a college. That finds `r format(nrow(SB$routes), big.mark = ",")` route and school pairs serving `r format(nrow(SB$by_school), big.mark = ",")` schools. Timetables do not say who a bus is for, so this will include a few commuter journeys and miss school contracts that are not in them.

For each school bus in the routed places, Output Areas within 400 m of a stop on its morning trips were routed to its school at every minute from 07:00, with every bus and walking available. That gives the last time a child can leave and still arrive by the bell, and how late they are if they miss it. Bells are not in the data, so the bell is set 15 minutes after the last school bus arrives.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sb-bh
#| tbl-cap: "Brighton and Hove schools with school buses: children living near a stop on one of them. Trips is morning school bus trips. Bell is inferred, 15 minutes after the last school bus. Uses it is the share whose last workable journey uses a school bus. Late is minutes late if that journey is missed, by the next best, also shown with a bell 10 minutes later. Walking is minutes at 3.6 km/h. Absence is all pupils, autumn and spring 2025/26."
sbt <- function(n) as.data.table(J$sbus$by_school)[net == n & oas >= 20] |> merge(as.data.table(SB$by_school)[, .(URN, routes, am_trips)], by = "URN", all.x = TRUE)
fmt_sb <- function(x) x[!is.nan(late)][order(-late)][, .(School = sub(" School$| Academy$| Community Academy$", "", name), Trips = am_trips, Bell = hm(bell), `Uses it` = sprintf("%.0f%%", uses_sb), Late = sprintf("%.1f", late), `Late, later bell` = sprintf("%.1f", late25), Walking = ifelse(is.na(walk_t), "120+", sprintf("%.0f", walk_t)), Absence = ifelse(is.na(overall), "–", sprintf("%.1f%%", overall)))] |> kt(align = "lrrrrrrr")
fmt_sb(sbt("bh"))
```

**Longhill stands apart in the city.** A child living near a stop who misses the last workable journey there arrives about `r sprintf("%.0f", sbv("Longhill High School", "late"))` minutes late, against `r sprintf("%.0f", min(sb_city$late))` to `r sprintf("%.0f", max(sb_city$late[sb_city$name != "Longhill High School"]))` minutes for the other city schools, and walking would take about `r sprintf("%.0f", sbv("Longhill High School", "walk_t"))` minutes. It also has the city's highest absence. The result depends on the bell: at 10 minutes later the penalty is `r sprintf("%.0f", sbv("Longhill High School", "late25"))` minutes. The inferred `r hm(sbv("Longhill High School", "bell"))` is close to the 08:20 in [the school's 2023 consultation](https://longhill.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/Timings-of-school-day.pdf), which should be confirmed for today. That document also notes that the school has one of the earliest starts in the area, and that a later start would go ahead only if the authority could provide the school buses, so the school day itself is set around them.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sb-ply
#| tbl-cap: "Plymouth, and nearby schools its children can reach by school bus, on the same basis as the Brighton and Hove table. Inferred bells are less reliable where a route arrives late in the morning, as at Millbay."
fmt_sb(sbt("plymouth"))
```

**Longhill is a striking case, not a pattern.** Across the `r nrow(sb_all)` schools in the routed places with school bus figures and published absence, the correlation between the penalty and absence is `r sprintf("%.2f", cor(sb_all$late, sb_all$overall))`, and for unauthorised absence `r sprintf("%.2f", cor(sb_all$late, sb_all$unauth))`. Several schools with larger penalties than Longhill's have low absence, usually with fewer disadvantaged pupils. Nor is having a school bus linked with absence across England (@tbl-sb-models). Having a bus is not the same as depending on one, and it often means the school has made sure that children can get there, so a null here does not mean that missing one is harmless. Still, these tests give no general support.

```{r}
#| label: fig-sb-models-ci
#| fig-cap: !expr paste("Schools with a school bus against others in the same authority, the estimates in the table below.", CI_NOTE)
#| fig-height: 3.4
SOn <- c(overall = "Overall absence", illness = "Illness", unauth = "Unauthorised", persistent = "Persistent absence (% of pupils)")
as.data.table(SB$models)[spec == "Has a school bus"][, .(row = sample, b, se, panel = SOn[outcome])] |> ci_plot("Points of absence", free_x = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sb-models
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Secondary schools in England, absence at schools with a school bus against other schools in the same authority, given distance, intake, ethnic make-up and kind of place, with t values. ", format(SB$n_schools, big.mark = ","), " schools, autumn and spring 2025/26, all pupils. High free school meals is the top quarter of schools.")
SO <- c(overall = "Overall absence", illness = "Illness", unauth = "Unauthorised", persistent = "Persistent absence (% of pupils)")
as.data.table(SB$models)[spec == "Has a school bus"][, v := sprintf("%+.2f (t = %.1f)", b, b / se)] |> dcast(outcome ~ sample, value.var = "v") |> (\(x) x[match(names(SO), outcome)][, .(`Kind of absence` = SO[outcome], `All schools`, Urban, Rural, `High free school meals` = `With high FSM`)])() |> kt(align = "lrrrr")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## The model behind this table

$$\text{absence}_s = \beta\,\text{has\_bus}_s + \lambda\,\log_2 \text{km}_s + \boldsymbol{\gamma}'\mathbf{z}_s + \pi_{\text{place}} + \alpha_a + \varepsilon_s$$

```r
# R/23_school_buses.R: every state secondary in England
feols(overall ~ has_bus + l2 + place + fsm + eal + wbri + ks2_c + z_l4 + sen_sup + ehcp + mobile + girls + age16 | la, data = d, cluster = ~la)
```

`has_bus` is 1 if a school bus route serves the school (see [the method](method.qmd#sec-journey-method)).
:::

### The climb {#sec-hills}

Straight lines also miss the hills. r5r's own elevation setting averages each street in both directions and did not change walking times in our tests, so the climb was measured directly, from OS Terrain 50 along each walking route, separately for the way to school and the way home.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-climb-places
#| tbl-cap: "Walking to the quickest school: metres climbed on the way there and on the way home, for the most deprived third of neighbourhoods (Dep.) and the rest (Rest), and the walking time to school with Tobler's hiking function, scaled to 3.6 km/h on the flat."
cw <- dcast(st3, place ~ t3, value.var = c("up_out", "up_back", "t_flat", "t_out", "t_back"))
cw[order(-up_back_dep)][, .(Place = place, `Dep.` = sprintf("%.0f", up_out_dep), Rest = sprintf("%.0f", up_out_rest), `Dep. ` = sprintf("%.0f", up_back_dep), `Rest ` = sprintf("%.0f", up_back_rest), `Dep.  ` = sprintf("%.1f", t_out_dep), `Rest  ` = sprintf("%.1f", t_out_rest), `Dep., flat` = sprintf("%.1f", t_flat_dep))] |> kt(align = "lrrrrrrr") |>
  kableExtra::add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Metres up, to school" = 2, "Metres up, home" = 2, "Minutes to school" = 3))
```

In Brighton and Hove, children in the most deprived third of neighbourhoods climb about `r sprintf("%.0f", js(BH, TRUE, "up_back"))` metres on the walk home, against `r sprintf("%.0f", js(BH, FALSE, "up_back"))` for the rest. That is the largest difference of the places here. Those children have both further to go and more to climb, which a straight line cannot show.

**A signal in the routed places did not hold across England.** In the schools of @tbl-journey-signal, more climb went clearly with more absence, more strongly than anything else tested. With so few schools that needed checking. Climb can be measured for all of England without routing, along the straight line from each of `r format(CB$n_oa, big.mark = ",")` Output Areas to its nearest school. In the routed places that matches the climb along the real route closely (r = `r sprintf("%.2f", CB$check$r_back)`).

```{r}
#| label: fig-climb-ci
#| fig-cap: !expr paste("Schools in England. Absence for each extra 10 metres climbed on the way home, the estimates in the table below.", CI_NOTE)
#| fig-height: 3.6
COn <- c(overall = "Overall absence", illness = "Illness", unauth = "Unauthorised", persistent = "Persistent absence (% of pupils)", abs_excess = "Above intake, 2021/22 to 2024/25")
as.data.table(CB$sch_models)[term == "up_back" & sample %in% c("All schools", "Urban", "Rural", "High free school meals", "Without Brighton and Hove")][, .(row = sample, b = 10 * b, se = 10 * se, panel = COn[outcome])] |>
  ci_plot("Points per 10 metres", ncol = 3, free_x = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-climb
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Secondary schools in England, absence for each extra 10 metres climbed on the way home by a school's nearest children, along a straight line, in the same authority, given distance, intake, ethnic make-up and kind of place, with t values. ", format(CB$n_sch, big.mark = ","), " schools. All pupils, autumn and spring 2025/26, except the last row.")
CO <- c(overall = "Overall absence", illness = "Illness", unauth = "Unauthorised", persistent = "Persistent absence (% of pupils)", abs_excess = "Above intake, 2021/22 to 2024/25")
as.data.table(CB$sch_models)[term == "up_back" & sample %in% c("All schools", "Urban", "Rural", "High free school meals", "Without Brighton and Hove")][, v := sprintf("%+.3f (t = %.1f)", 10 * b, b / se)] |> dcast(outcome ~ sample, value.var = "v") |> (\(x) x[match(names(CO), outcome)][, .(`Kind of absence` = CO[outcome], `All schools`, Urban, Rural, `High free school meals`, `Without Brighton and Hove`)])() |> kt(align = "lrrrrr")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## The model behind this table

$$\text{absence}_s = \beta\,\text{up\_back}_s + \lambda\,\log_2 \text{km}_s + \boldsymbol{\gamma}'\mathbf{z}_s + \alpha_a + \varepsilon_s$$

```r
# R/25_climb.R: every state secondary in England
feols(overall ~ up_back + l2 + fsm + eal + wbri + ks2_c + z_l4 + sen_sup + ehcp + mobile + girls + age16 + place | la, data = S, cluster = ~la)
```

`up_back` is the child-weighted mean metres climbed on the way home, along the straight line from each of the school's nearest Output Areas; the table gives $10\beta$.
:::

Across England the link for overall absence is small and not clear: `r sprintf("%+.3f", 10 * cbs("overall"))` points for each extra 10 metres (t = `r sprintf("%.1f", cbs("overall") / cbs("overall", "se"))`), and within authorities by home neighbourhood `r sprintf("%+.3f", 10 * cbc("overall"))` (t = `r sprintf("%.1f", cbc("overall") / cbc("overall", "se"))`). There is a small link with illness absence (t = `r sprintf("%.1f", cbs("illness") / cbs("illness", "se"))`), clearer for schools near major towns and cities, and none with unauthorised absence. Between authorities the link for disadvantaged pupils is larger, given their ethnic mix (`r sprintf("%+.2f", 10 * cbl("dis", "And ethnic mix of the group"))` per 10 metres, t = `r sprintf("%.1f", cbl("dis", "And ethnic mix of the group") / cbl("dis", "And ethnic mix of the group", "se"))`; non-disadvantaged pupils `r sprintf("%+.2f", 10 * cbl("non", "And ethnic mix of the group"))`, all pupils `r sprintf("%+.2f", 10 * cbl("all", "And ethnic mix of the group"))`), and falls by about half given region. So the first result looks largely local, with at most a small general link. Straight lines do understate climb, so a modest effect could still be there, and with climb along real walking routes in the 109 mostly urban authorities it is [clearer](#sec-la-time).

### Does time say more than distance about absence? {#sec-time-absence}

Among these places it cannot be answered: they include only `r sum(!is.na(J$abs_la$abs_dis))` authorities with published absence. @tbl-journey-absence sets them side by side, for all three groups of pupils, without modelling them. The test across all the mostly urban authorities is [below](#sec-la-time).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-journey-absence
#| tbl-cap: "Authorities routed so far: distance and journey time from the most deprived third of neighbourhoods, and absence in state-funded secondary schools, 2024/25. DfE publishes absence by disadvantage for authorities, so Hastings has none."
J$abs_la |> arrange(desc(t_dep)) |> transmute(Place = place, `Straight line (km)` = sprintf("%.2f", km_dep), `Walking and bus (min)` = sprintf("%.1f", t_dep), `All pupils` = ifelse(is.na(abs_all), "–", sprintf("%.1f%%", abs_all)), Disadvantaged = ifelse(is.na(abs_dis), "–", sprintf("%.1f%%", abs_dis)), `Non-disadvantaged` = ifelse(is.na(abs_non), "–", sprintf("%.1f%%", abs_non))) |> kt(align = "lrrrrr")
```

DfE's file by home neighbourhood gives a little more, by comparing tenths within these authorities (`r J$cell_models$n[1]` groups of pupils, all pupils, 2023/24 and 2024/25). Distance and time point the same way and are hard to tell apart: for one standard deviation more, overall absence is `r sprintf("%.2f", jc("overall", "km"))` points higher on straight-line distance, `r sprintf("%.2f", jc("overall", "t_walk"))` on walking time and `r sprintf("%.2f", jc("overall", "t_bus"))` on walking and bus time. Persistent absence is `r sprintf("%.1f", jc("persistent", "km"))`, `r sprintf("%.1f", jc("persistent", "t_walk"))` and `r sprintf("%.1f", jc("persistent", "t_bus"))` points of pupils. With so few authorities these are descriptive. The [109 mostly urban authorities](#sec-la-time) give the proper test.

### How far to trust these times {#sec-journey-limits}

- **Against the city's model.** On that model's settings, times for `r J$validate$lsoas` Brighton and Hove neighbourhoods correlate at `r sprintf("%.2f", J$validate$r)` with [the city's school system model](https://adamdennett.github.io/bh-school-system/), with a mean of `r sprintf("%.1f", J$validate$mean_new)` minutes against `r sprintf("%.1f", J$validate$mean_old)` and a typical difference of `r sprintf("%.1f", J$validate$mae)` minutes. The difference between deprived neighbourhoods and the rest is `r sprintf("%.1f", J$validate$gap_new)` minutes here and `r sprintf("%.1f", J$validate$gap_old)` there. The model uses an older timetable, a set list of schools and an earlier departure for Longhill, and these have not been separated. Its simulator's 4 minute difference is another measure again: it follows children to the school they are allocated and compares disadvantaged children with others.
- **Walking speed.** r5r's default is 3.6 km/h, slow for a teenager, and is kept to match the city's model. At 4.8 km/h Brighton and Hove's difference with buses is `r sprintf("%.1f", jt(BH, "gap", "walk_bus_f"))` minutes, so the result does not depend on it.
- **Buses only.** Rail, the Tube, the DLR and school-only services that are not in the timetable files are missing. That matters most in Newham and Tower Hamlets, where it would shorten journeys, not lengthen them.
- **One day.** Departures from 07:45 to 08:15 on one Tuesday, taking the median. Real journeys depend on when a school starts.
- **The quickest school is not always the school attended.** Children go further than this, more so where choice or catchments send them elsewhere. Who can get a place at the quickest school is not considered.
- **Boundaries.** Each place is a district, with schools up to 15 km beyond it. Hastings, Blackpool and others have few schools nearby, and Plymouth and Bristol's networks include neighbouring counties.

## Journeys in the 109 mostly urban authorities {#sec-la-journeys}

The nine places above show that Brighton and Hove stands out, but they are too few to say whether journeys matter for absence. So the routing was repeated for all `r nrow(PL)` [mostly urban authorities](#sec-urban), London's 32 boroughs included: `r format(JL$n_oas, big.mark = ",")` Output Areas on `r nrow(JL$nets)` networks, routed to every state secondary school within reach on the same Tuesday, `r format(JL$flat_meta$date[1], "%e %B %Y")`, with the same settings. Where the two overlap, the times are identical. Sources, networks and checks are in [the methodology](method.qmd#sec-la-routing-method).

As before, journeys go to each neighbourhood's *quickest* school, deprivation is of the neighbourhood, and the timetables are buses only. Rail, the Underground, Metro and trams are missing, which matters most in London, Greater Manchester, Tyne and Wear, the West Midlands, Sheffield and Nottingham. In all of them the missing services would shorten journeys.

### Is Brighton and Hove unusual? {#sec-la-bh}

```{r}
#| label: fig-la-gap
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("How much further the most deprived third of each authority's neighbourhoods is from a school than the rest, in straight-line kilometres and in minutes by walking and bus, for the ", nrow(PL), " mostly urban authorities. The line is a simple fit. Above zero on either axis, the deprived neighbourhoods are further away.")
#| fig-height: 5
gp_dat <- PL |> mutate(who = case_when(la == BH ~ BH, london ~ "London borough", TRUE ~ "Elsewhere"))
gp_lab <- gp_dat |> arrange(desc(t_bus_gap)) |> slice(1:6) |> bind_rows(gp_dat |> arrange(t_bus_gap) |> slice(1:2))
ggplot(gp_dat, aes(km1_gap, t_bus_gap)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = LIGHT) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = LIGHT) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, colour = GREY, linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = who, size = who == BH)) + geom_text_repel(data = gp_lab, aes(label = la), size = 3.2, colour = INK, min.segment.length = 0) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(c(BPURPLE, BLUE, GREY), c(BH, "London borough", "Elsewhere")), name = NULL) + scale_size_manual(values = c(1.8, 3.2), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Extra straight-line km for the deprived third", y = "Extra minutes by walking and bus") + theme_note()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-la-outlier
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Brighton and Hove among the ", nrow(PL), " mostly urban authorities. Rank 1 is the highest; for minutes per kilometre, the slowest. The last column gives the first authority, or the next where Brighton and Hove is first. The deprived third is the most deprived third of each authority's neighbourhoods on Census household deprivation.")
OLM <- c("t_bus_gap", "t_bus_igap", "t_bus_dgap", "t3_bus_gap", "t_open_gap", "t_walk_gap", "km1_gap", "t_bus_dep", "t_bus_rest", "over30_dep", "mpk_dep", "p_two_dep", "wait_dep", "late_dep", "up_back_dep")
JL$outlier_all[match(OLM, measure)][, .(Measure = label, `Brighton and Hove` = mapply(function(v, d) formatC(v, format = "f", digits = d), bh, digits),
  Rank = paste0(rank, " of ", n), Median = mapply(function(v, d) formatC(v, format = "f", digits = d), median, digits),
  `First, or next` = ifelse(top == BH, paste0(next_, " (", mapply(function(v, d) formatC(v, format = "f", digits = d), next_v, digits), ")"), paste0(top, " (", mapply(function(v, d) formatC(v, format = "f", digits = d), top_v, digits), ")")))] |> kt(align = "lrrrl")
```

**No other authority's deprived neighbourhoods are as far from a school.** By walking and bus, children in the most deprived third of Brighton and Hove's neighbourhoods are `r sprintf("%.1f", ol("t_bus_gap"))` minutes further from a school than the rest of the city, the largest gap of the `r nrow(PL)`. Next are `r and_list(sprintf("%s (%.1f)", gap_top$la[2:3], gap_top$t_bus_gap[2:3]))`. In the median authority the deprived third is `r sprintf("%.1f", -ol("t_bus_gap", "median"))` minutes *nearer*, and only `r sum(PL$t_bus_gap > 0)` of the `r nrow(PL)` have it further at all. The city is first on every version of the gap in @tbl-la-outlier but one: to the quickest school that is neither selective nor faith, it is second, just behind Tameside. Among the `r nrow(dense)` densest authorities, the next largest gap is `r sprintf("%.1f", dense$t_bus_gap[2])` minutes, in `r dense$la[2]`.

**It is mostly distance, not slow buses.** Across the `r nrow(PL)` authorities the gap in minutes follows the gap in kilometres closely (r = `r sprintf("%.2f", JL$cor_la$r_gap)`), and Brighton and Hove sits close to the line in @fig-la-gap: its `r sprintf("%.2f", ol("km1_gap"))` km predicts `r sprintf("%.1f", adj_v("t_bus_gap", "km1_gap", 109, "expected"))` minutes. Per kilometre, the journeys from its deprived neighbourhoods are among the quickest anywhere (`r sprintf("%.1f", ol("mpk_dep"))` minutes, against a median of `r sprintf("%.1f", ol("mpk_dep", "median"))`). The schools are unusually far away; the buses are not unusually slow.

**But the journeys need the most changes.** `r sprintf("%.0f%%", ol("p_two_dep"))` of journeys from its deprived third need two or more buses, against a median of `r sprintf("%.0f%%", ol("p_two_dep", "median"))`, and the next highest is `r ol("p_two_dep", "next_")` (`r sprintf("%.0f%%", ol("p_two_dep", "next_v"))`). That is more than distance and density predict (`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * adj_v("p_two_dep", "km1_dep + log_density", 109, "expected"))`), and only `r strsplit(adj_v("p_two_dep", "km1_dep + log_density", 109, "top"), "; ")[[1]][1]` is further above its prediction. Waiting is the longest too, and so is the climb on the walk home, `r sprintf("%.0f", ol("up_back_dep"))` metres against a median of `r sprintf("%.0f", ol("up_back_dep", "median"))`.

In absolute terms, children in the city's deprived neighbourhoods are `r sprintf("%.1f", ol("t_bus_dep"))` minutes from a school, `r ord(ol("t_bus_dep", "rank"))` longest of the `r nrow(PL)`, behind `r and_list(JL$outlier_all[measure == "t_bus_dep", top])` and Barnsley, and `r sprintf("%.0f%%", ol("over30_dep"))` of them are more than 30 minutes away. The rest of the city is average (`r ord(ol("t_bus_rest", "rank"))`). The earlier work found the same thing among nine places, and it holds among `r nrow(PL)`.

### What these journeys look like {#sec-route-examples}

Averages are hard to picture. @fig-route-examples shows real routes on the same networks, at the same scale: from Whitehawk, to its quickest school and to Dorothy Stringer, where the 2024 map sends more of its children; and, in Brighton and Hove and three comparator cities, a typical journey for a deprived neighbourhood. Each example is chosen by rule, not by eye: the Output Area whose time is nearest the mean for Whitehawk, or for the city's most deprived third, among those whose quickest school is open to all. Each was routed every five minutes from 07:45 to 08:15 and the departure with the median time is shown ([method](method.qmd#sec-route-examples-method)).

```{r}
#| label: fig-route-examples
#| fig-cap: !expr paste("Example journeys to school by walking and bus, all at the same scale. Purple lines are buses, with their route numbers, and dashed lines are walking; the dark dot is home and the blue square the school.", BASEMAP_CREDIT, ROUTE_CREDIT)
#| fig-height: 14
fig_route_examples()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-route-anatomy
#| fig-cap: "What each example journey is made of, in minutes from leaving home, with the metres climbed on foot. The tick is the mean time for the group the example stands for (Whitehawk, or the city's most deprived third), which also counts waiting at home for the first bus, so it is a little longer."
#| fig-height: 3.6
fig_route_anatomy()
```

**Elsewhere, a typical deprived neighbourhood's journey is a walk, or a short ride on one bus.** In Bristol, Southampton and Plymouth it takes `r sprintf("%.0f", min(RX$summary$total[startsWith(RX$summary$id, "typ_") & RX$summary$id != "typ_sussex"]))` to `r sprintf("%.0f", max(RX$summary$total[startsWith(RX$summary$id, "typ_") & RX$summary$id != "typ_sussex"]))` minutes, to a school about a kilometre away in a straight line. In Brighton and Hove the typical deprived journey already takes two buses. From Whitehawk it takes two buses across the city, about `r sprintf("%.0f", RX$summary[id == "wh_quick", total])` minutes to the quickest school and `r sprintf("%.0f", RX$summary[id == "wh_ds", total])` to Dorothy Stringer, with `r sprintf("%.0f", RX$summary[id == "wh_ds", climb])` metres to climb on foot on the second. Both Whitehawk journeys change buses in the city centre.

### Does the journey say more than distance about absence? {#sec-la-time}

With `r nrow(PL)` authorities the tests above can be rerun on journeys. @tbl-la-tests sets out the three designs: authorities for disadvantaged pupils, home neighbourhoods within authorities for all pupils, and schools within authorities for all pupils, with primary absence as the falsification test.

```{r}
#| label: fig-la-tests-ci
#| fig-cap: !expr paste("The tests in the table below. Secondary absence for one standard deviation more of each feature of the journey, in each design. Primary is the falsification test.", CI_NOTE)
#| fig-height: 6.5
TTn <- c(km = "Straight-line distance", t_bus = "Minutes by walking and bus", t_walk = "Minutes walking", two_share = "Share needing two or more buses", wait = "Minutes waiting", late = "Minutes late if the last journey is missed", up_back = "Metres climbed walking home")
ltn <- c(km = "km1_dep", t_bus = "t_bus_dep", t_walk = "t_walk_dep", two_share = "p_two_dep", wait = "wait_dep", late = "late_dep", up_back = "up_back_dep")
sdv <- function(x) if (nrow(x)) tibble(b = x$b * x$sd_x, se = x$se * x$sd_x) else tibble(b = NA_real_, se = NA_real_)
bind_rows(lapply(names(TTn), function(tm) bind_rows(
  sdv(JL$la_models[term == ltn[[tm]] & group == "dis" & ctrl == "And every control" & sample == "All 109" & phase == "sec" & outcome == "overall"]) |> mutate(panel = "Authorities, disadvantaged"),
  sdv(JL$la_given[term == ltn[[tm]] & group == "dis" & ctrl == "And every control" & sample == "All 109" & phase == "sec"]) |> mutate(panel = "Authorities, given km"),
  sdv(JL$la_models[term == ltn[[tm]] & group == "dis" & ctrl == "And every control" & sample == "All 109" & phase == "pri" & outcome == "overall"]) |> mutate(panel = "Authorities, primary"),
  sdv(JL$cell_models[term == tm & sample == "All authorities" & ctrl == "And Census character" & phase == "sec" & outcome == "overall"]) |> mutate(panel = "Tenths, within authority"),
  sdv(JL$cell_models[term == tm & sample == "All authorities" & ctrl == "And straight-line km" & phase == "sec" & outcome == "overall"]) |> mutate(panel = "Tenths, given km"),
  sdv(JL$school_models[term == ifelse(tm == "km", "l2", tm) & sample == "All schools" & outcome == "overall"]) |> mutate(panel = "Schools, given distance")) |>
  mutate(row = TTn[[tm]]))) |> filter(!(row == TTn[["km"]] & panel %in% c("Authorities, given km", "Tenths, given km"))) |>
  mutate(panel = factor(panel, c("Authorities, disadvantaged", "Authorities, given km", "Authorities, primary", "Tenths, within authority", "Tenths, given km", "Schools, given distance"))) |>
  ci_plot("Points of absence per standard deviation", ncol = 3, wrap = 26)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-la-tests
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Secondary absence for one standard deviation more of each feature of the journeys from the most deprived third of neighbourhoods (authorities) or from each neighbourhood (tenths and schools), with t values in brackets. Authorities are disadvantaged pupils, ", nrow(PL), " authorities, 2018/19 to 2024/25, every control. Tenths are all pupils by IDACI tenth of home neighbourhood, within authority, 2023/24 and 2024/25, given Census character. Schools are all pupils, within authority, given intake and distance, autumn and spring 2025/26. Given km adds straight-line distance. Primary is the same authority model for primary absence.")
TT <- c(km = "Straight-line distance", t_bus = "Minutes by walking and bus", t_walk = "Minutes walking", two_share = "Share needing two or more buses", wait = "Minutes waiting", late = "Minutes late if the last journey is missed", up_back = "Metres climbed walking home")
la_term <- c(km = "km1_dep", t_bus = "t_bus_dep", t_walk = "t_walk_dep", two_share = "p_two_dep", wait = "wait_dep", late = "late_dep", up_back = "up_back_dep")
fmt_t <- function(b, se, sd) ifelse(is.na(b), "–", sprintf("%+.2f (%.1f)", b * sd, b / se))
la_v <- function(tm, ph = "sec") { x <- JL$la_models[term == la_term[[tm]] & group == "dis" & ctrl == "And every control" & sample == "All 109" & phase == ph & outcome == "overall"]; fmt_t(x$b, x$se, x$sd_x) }
lg_v <- function(tm) { if (tm == "km") return("–"); x <- JL$la_given[term == la_term[[tm]] & group == "dis" & ctrl == "And every control" & sample == "All 109" & phase == "sec"]; fmt_t(x$b, x$se, x$sd_x) }
ce_v <- function(tm, ct) { if (tm == "km" && ct == "And straight-line km") return("–"); x <- JL$cell_models[term == tm & sample == "All authorities" & ctrl == ct & phase == "sec" & outcome == "overall"]; fmt_t(x$b, x$se, x$sd_x) }
sc_v <- function(tm) { x <- JL$school_models[term == ifelse(tm == "km", "l2", tm) & sample == "All schools" & outcome == "overall"]; fmt_t(x$b, x$se, x$sd_x) }
data.table(`Feature of the journey` = TT, Alone = sapply(names(TT), la_v), `Given km` = sapply(names(TT), lg_v), Primary = sapply(names(TT), la_v, ph = "pri"),
           `Alone ` = sapply(names(TT), ce_v, ct = "And Census character"), `Given km ` = sapply(names(TT), ce_v, ct = "And straight-line km"), `Given km  ` = sapply(names(TT), sc_v)) |>
  kt(align = "lrrrrrr") |> kableExtra::add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Authorities, disadvantaged" = 3, "Tenths, within authority" = 2, "Schools" = 1))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## The model behind this table

$$\begin{aligned}
\textbf{Authorities:}\quad & \text{absence}^{\text{dis}}_{a,t} = \beta\,x_a\,[+\,\lambda\,\text{km1\_dep}_a] + \boldsymbol{\gamma}'\mathbf{x}_{a,t} + \tau_t + \varepsilon_{a,t}\\
\textbf{Tenths:}\quad & \text{absence}_{a,d,t} = \beta\,x_{a,d}\,[+\,\lambda\,\text{km}_{a,d}] + \boldsymbol{\gamma}'\mathbf{c}_{a,d} + \alpha_{a,t} + \delta_{d,t} + \varepsilon_{a,d,t}\\
\textbf{Schools:}\quad & \text{absence}_s = \beta\,x_s + \lambda\,\log_2\text{km}_s + \boldsymbol{\gamma}'\mathbf{z}_s + \alpha_a + \varepsilon_s
\end{aligned}$$

```r
# R/29_la_analysis.R; x is the journey feature in the row (t_bus_dep, t_walk_dep, p_two_dep, wait_dep, late_dep, up_back_dep, ...)
feols(overall ~ x [+ km1_dep] + share + urban_share + eth_wb + eth_asian + eth_black + eth_mixed + gor +
        graduates + bad_health + white_british + social_rent + no_car + deprived + log_density +
        sen_sup + ehcp + ks2_c + eal + wbri + mobile | tp, data = A, cluster = ~la)                     # authorities, disadvantaged
feols(overall ~ x [+ km] + urban_c + dens_c + grad_c + wbri_c + nocar_c + social_c + bad_c | la^tp + dec^tp,
      data = B, weights = ~enrol, cluster = ~la)                                                       # tenths, all pupils
feols(overall ~ x + l2 + fsm + eal + wbri + ks2_c + z_l4 + sen_sup + ehcp + mobile + girls + age16 + place | la,
      data = S, cluster = ~la)                                                                         # schools, all pupils
```

Journey features for authorities are of the most deprived third of neighbourhoods; for tenths and schools, of the Output Areas in them. Each figure is $\beta$ times the standard deviation of $x$, with its t value. "Primary" is the authority model with primary absence on the left.
:::

- **Distance holds up, most clearly outside London.** For disadvantaged pupils, with every control, absence is `r sprintf("%.1f", lam("km1_dep"))` points higher for each extra kilometre between the deprived third and a school (t = `r sprintf("%.1f", lat("km1_dep"))`), `r sprintf("%.1f", lam("km1_dep", s = "Without London"))` outside London (t = `r sprintf("%.1f", lat("km1_dep", s = "Without London"))`) and `r sprintf("%.1f", lam("km1_dep", s = "Without Brighton and Hove"))` without Brighton and Hove (t = `r sprintf("%.1f", lat("km1_dep", s = "Without Brighton and Hove"))`). It is smaller for non-disadvantaged pupils (`r sprintf("%.1f", lam("km1_dep", "non"))`, t = `r sprintf("%.1f", lat("km1_dep", "non"))`) and all pupils (`r sprintf("%.1f", lam("km1_dep", "all"))`, t = `r sprintf("%.1f", lat("km1_dep", "all"))`), and much weaker in primary (`r sprintf("%.1f", lam("km1_dep", ph = "pri"))`, t = `r sprintf("%.1f", lat("km1_dep", ph = "pri"))`). This matches the straight-line results [above](#sec-urban).
- **Time does not beat distance.** Minutes and kilometres are too closely tied to separate (r = `r sprintf("%.2f", JL$cor_la$r_t_km)` across authorities, `r sprintf("%.2f", JL$sep$r_within)` within them). Put in the same model for disadvantaged pupils, distance keeps its link (t = `r sprintf("%.1f", ha("b_km") / ha("se_km"))`) and time loses its own (t = `r sprintf("%.1f", ha("b_t") / ha("se_t"))`). Within authorities neither wins.
- **Changes of bus, waiting and the penalty for a missed bus add nothing beyond distance.** With fewer controls each goes with more absence across authorities, because long journeys have more of them, but given distance none keeps a clear link.
- **The climb is the one feature that keeps appearing.** Across authorities it goes with disadvantaged absence given every control (t = `r sprintf("%.1f", lat("up_back_dep"))`, and `r sprintf("%.1f", lam("up_back_dep", s = "Without Brighton and Hove") / lam("up_back_dep", s = "Without Brighton and Hove", col = "se"))` without Brighton and Hove), and still about t = `r sprintf("%.1f", lg_t("up_back_dep"))` given distance. Within authorities it is t = `r sprintf("%.1f", cl_t("up_back", "And straight-line km"))` given distance, and in primary there is nothing. That is suggestive, not established: this page runs many tests, and climb along the straight line [did not hold](#sec-hills) between schools across England.

### Places to stop on the way {#sec-la-poi}

If a journey matters partly for what it passes, a child who gets off a bus beside a row of shops and cafés has more chances to go elsewhere than one who gets off at the school gate. So `r format(JL$poi$n, big.mark = ",")` points of interest were taken from OpenStreetMap, in five groups: food and drink, shops, leisure, open space and civic places. Schools, transport and parking are left out. Each was counted within 200 metres of the stop where a journey starts, every change of bus and the last stop, and within 50 metres of the walking route and the walking legs of bus journeys. The points of interest within 400 metres of home are a control, because a child in a busy place passes busy places whatever their journey. The tags and checks are in [the methodology](method.qmd#sec-poi-method).

```{r}
#| label: fig-la-poi-ci
#| fig-cap: !expr paste("The tests in the table below. Absence for one standard deviation more points of interest on the way, in each design.", CI_NOTE)
#| fig-height: 5.8
PTn <- c(walk50_any = "Along the walking route, within 50 m", leg50_any = "Along walking legs of bus journeys, within 50 m", p_any_board = "At the first stop, within 200 m", p_any_change = "At changes of bus, within 200 m", p_any_alight = "At the last stop, within 200 m")
bind_rows(lapply(names(PTn), function(tm) bind_rows(
  sdv(JL$la_models[term == paste0(tm, "_dep") & group == "dis" & ctrl == "And every control" & sample == "All 109" & phase == "sec" & outcome == "overall"]) |> mutate(panel = "Authorities, secondary"),
  sdv(JL$la_models[term == paste0(tm, "_dep") & group == "dis" & ctrl == "And every control" & sample == "All 109" & phase == "pri" & outcome == "overall"]) |> mutate(panel = "Authorities, primary"),
  sdv(JL$cell_models[term == tm & sample == "All authorities" & ctrl == "And changes of bus" & phase == "sec" & outcome == "overall"]) |> mutate(panel = "Tenths, secondary"),
  sdv(JL$cell_models[term == tm & sample == "All authorities" & ctrl == "And changes of bus" & phase == "pri" & outcome == "overall"]) |> mutate(panel = "Tenths, primary"),
  sdv(JL$cell_models[term == tm & sample == "Without London" & ctrl == "And changes of bus" & phase == "sec" & outcome == "overall"]) |> mutate(panel = "Tenths, outside London"),
  sdv(JL$school_models[term == tm & sample == "All schools" & outcome == "overall"]) |> mutate(panel = "Schools")) |>
  mutate(row = PTn[[tm]]))) |> ci_plot("Points of absence per standard deviation", ncol = 3, wrap = 26)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-la-poi
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Absence for one standard deviation more points of interest on the way to the quickest school, with t values in brackets, on the same designs as the table above. Authorities are disadvantaged pupils, every control. Tenths are all pupils, within authority, given distance, Census character, points of interest near home, the share needing two or more buses and buses per journey. Schools are all pupils, within authority, given intake and distance. OpenStreetMap, ", format(JL$poi$osm_date, "%e %B %Y"), ".")
PT <- c(walk50_any = "Along the walking route, within 50 m", leg50_any = "Along walking legs of bus journeys, within 50 m", p_any_board = "At the first stop, within 200 m", p_any_change = "At changes of bus, within 200 m", p_any_alight = "At the last stop, within 200 m")
la_p <- function(tm, ph) { x <- JL$la_models[term == paste0(tm, "_dep") & group == "dis" & ctrl == "And every control" & sample == "All 109" & phase == ph & outcome == "overall"]; fmt_t(x$b, x$se, x$sd_x) }
ce_p <- function(tm, ph, s = "All authorities") { x <- JL$cell_models[term == tm & sample == s & ctrl == "And changes of bus" & phase == ph & outcome == "overall"]; fmt_t(x$b, x$se, x$sd_x) }
data.table(`Points of interest` = PT, Secondary = sapply(names(PT), la_p, ph = "sec"), Primary = sapply(names(PT), la_p, ph = "pri"),
```
